title.zh: 卷一百八十一 列傳第六十八: 元明善 虞集 揭傒斯 黃溍
title.en: Volume 181 Biographies 68: Yuan Mingshan, Yu Ji, Jie Xisi, Huang Jin
title.raw: 卷一百八十一 列傳第六十八: 元明善 虞集 揭傒斯 黃溍 Volume 181 Biographies 68: Yuan Mingshan, Yu Ji, Jie Xisi, Huang Jin

sentences.zh: 元明善

translations.literal: Yuan Mingshan
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Mingshan

sentences.zh: 元明善，字復初，大名清河人。

translations.literal: Yuan Mingshan, styled Fuchu, was a man of Qinghe in Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Mingshan, whose style was Fuchu, came from Qinghe in Daming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 其先蓋拓跋魏之裔，居清河者，至明善四世矣。

translations.literal: His ancestors were probably descendants of the Tuoba Northern Wei; those dwelling in Qinghe had reached the fourth generation by Mingshan.
translations.idiomatic: His family were said to be descendants of the Tuoba Northern Wei; by Mingshan's time they had lived in Qinghe for four generations.

sentences.zh: 明善資穎悟絕，出讀書，過目輒記，諸經皆有師法，而尤深於《春秋》。

translations.literal: Mingshan's native quickness of understanding was extraordinary; when he went out to read books, whatever passed before his eyes he at once remembered. In all the Classics he had received systematic instruction, but he was especially deep in the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: Mingshan was extraordinarily quick-witted: whatever he read, he remembered at a glance. He had proper instruction in all the Classics, but was especially accomplished in the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 弱冠遊吳中，已名能文章。

translations.literal: At twenty he traveled in Wu, and was already famed for ability in literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: In his early twenties he traveled through the Wu region and was already known as a capable writer.

sentences.zh: 浙東使者薦為安豐、建康兩學正。

translations.literal: The envoy to Zhedong recommended him as academic director of the Anfeng and Jian'ang schools.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhedong circuit envoy recommended him as director of the Anfeng and Jian'ang schools.

sentences.zh: 辟掾，行樞密院。

translations.literal: He was recruited as a clerk and served at the traveling Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was recruited as a clerk and served at the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時董士選僉院事，待之若賓友，不敢以曹屬御之。

translations.literal: At the time Dong Shixuan was vice-director of the bureau; he treated Mingshan as a guest and friend and did not dare handle him as an ordinary subordinate.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Dong Shixuan was vice-director of the bureau; he treated Mingshan as a guest and friend and would not deal with him as a routine clerk.

sentences.zh: 及士選升江西左丞，又辟為省掾。

translations.literal: When Shixuan was promoted to Left Vice Governor of Jiangxi, he again recruited Mingshan as a provincial clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Shixuan was promoted to Left Vice Governor of Jiangxi, he recruited Mingshan again as a provincial clerk.

sentences.zh: 會贛州賊劉貴反，明善從士選將兵討之，擒賊三百人。

translations.literal: It happened that the bandit Liu Gui rebelled in Ganzhou; Mingshan followed Shixuan in leading troops to suppress him and captured three hundred rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandit Liu Gui rebelled in Ganzhou, Mingshan accompanied Shixuan in leading troops against him and captured three hundred rebels.

sentences.zh: 明善議緩詿誤，得全活者百三十人。

translations.literal: Mingshan argued for leniency in cases of obstruction and delay, and one hundred thirty persons were spared alive.
translations.idiomatic: Mingshan urged leniency for those charged with obstruction or delay, and one hundred thirty people were spared.

sentences.zh: 一日，將佐白：「宜多戮俘獲，及屍一切死者，以張軍聲。」

translations.literal: One day the officers reported: 'We ought to slaughter many captives, and all the dead upon the field as well, to magnify the army's renown.'
translations.idiomatic: One day his officers reported, "We ought to slaughter many captives, and all the dead upon the field as well, to magnify the army's renown."

sentences.zh: 明善固爭，以為王者之師，恭行天罰，小丑跳梁，戮其渠魁可爾，民何辜焉。

translations.literal: Mingshan firmly opposed this, holding that the army of a True King, reverently executing Heaven's punishment, need only execute the ringleaders of petty rabble leaping about—what guilt had the common people?
translations.idiomatic: Mingshan objected firmly, arguing that the army of a true king, reverently carrying out Heaven's punishment, need only cut down the ringleaders of a petty uprising; the common people were innocent.

sentences.zh: 既又得賊所書贛、吉民丁十萬於籍者，有司喜，欲滋蔓為利，明善請火其籍以滅跡，二郡遂安。

translations.literal: They also obtained rebel documents listing one hundred thousand men of Gan and Ji on the register; officials rejoiced and wished to extend the investigation for profit. Mingshan requested that the register be burned to efface the trace, and the two prefectures were thereafter at peace.
translations.idiomatic: They also found rebel registers listing one hundred thousand men from Gan and Ji; officials were pleased and wanted to extend the inquiry for profit. Mingshan asked that the registers be burned to erase the evidence, and the two circuits were thereafter pacified.

sentences.zh: 陞掾南行臺。

translations.literal: He was promoted to clerk of the Southern Branch Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to clerk of the Southern Branch Censorate.

sentences.zh: 未幾，授樞密院照磨。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed registrar of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed registrar of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 轉中書左曹掾，掾曹無留事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to clerk in the Left Department of the Secretariat; no matters remained pending in that office.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to clerk in the Left Department of the Secretariat, where no business was left pending.

sentences.zh: 始，明善在江西時，張瑄為其省參政，明善有馬，駿而瘠，瑄假為從騎，久益壯，瑄愛之，致米三十斛酬其直。

translations.literal: Earlier, while Mingshan was in Jiangxi, Zhang Xuan was provincial administrator there. Mingshan had a horse—spirited but lean—and Xuan borrowed it for his escort; in time it grew stronger, and Xuan came to love it, sending thirty hu of rice as payment for its price.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Mingshan was in Jiangxi, Zhang Xuan was the provincial administrator. Mingshan owned a spirited but lean horse, which Xuan borrowed for his escort; over time it grew stronger, and Xuan grew fond of it and sent thirty hu of rice as payment.

sentences.zh: 後瑄敗，江浙行省籍其家，得金谷之簿，書「米三十斛送元復初」，不言以酬馬直，明善坐免。

translations.literal: Later Xuan fell from grace; the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat inventoried his household and obtained his account book of grain and money, which recorded 'thirty hu of rice sent to Yuan Fuchu' without stating it was payment for the horse. Mingshan was dismissed on this charge.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Xuan fell from power, the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat inventoried his estate and found an account book recording 'thirty hu of rice sent to Yuan Fuchu' without noting it was payment for the horse. Mingshan was dismissed on that account.

sentences.zh: 久之，有為辨白其事者，乃復掾省曹。

translations.literal: After some time someone argued to clear him of the matter, and he was restored to his clerkship in the provincial office.
translations.idiomatic: After some time someone cleared him of the charge, and he was restored to his clerkship in the provincial office.

sentences.zh: 仁宗居東宮，首擢為太子文學。

translations.literal: When the Renzong Emperor was heir apparent, he first elevated Mingshan to Literary Instructor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: While Renzong was still heir apparent, he first appointed Mingshan Literary Instructor of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 及即位，改翰林待制。

translations.literal: When the emperor acceded, he was changed to Attendant Draftsman at the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong took the throne, Mingshan was made Attendant Draftsman at the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 與修成宗、順宗《實錄》，升翰林直學士。

translations.literal: He participated in compiling the Veritable Records of Emperor Chengzong and Emperor Shunzong, and was promoted to Direct Academician of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He helped compile the Veritable Records of Emperors Chengzong and Shunzong and was promoted to Direct Academician of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 詔節《尚書》經文，譯其關政要者以進。

translations.literal: An edict ordered abridgment of the Book of Documents and translation of passages bearing on governance for presentation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Book of Documents abridged and passages relevant to governance translated and submitted.

sentences.zh: 明善舉宋忠臣子集賢直學士文升同譯潤，許之。

translations.literal: Mingshan recommended the Song loyalist's son Wen Sheng, Direct Academician of the Academy of Assembled Worthies, to assist in translation and polishing; his recommendation was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Mingshan recommended Wen Sheng, son of a Song loyalist and Direct Academician of the Academy of Assembled Worthies, to assist in translation and polishing; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 書成，每奏一篇，帝必稱善，曰：「二帝三王之道，非卿莫聞也。」

translations.literal: When the work was finished, each time a section was submitted the emperor invariably praised it, saying: 'The way of the Two Emperors and Three Kings—not unless you had heard it from you, sir.'
translations.idiomatic: When the work was finished, each section the emperor heard drew his praise: 'The way of the Two Emperors and Three Kings—only you could teach it to us.'

sentences.zh: 興聖太后既受尊號，廷臣請因肆赦，明善曰：「數赦，非善人之福，宥過可也。」

translations.literal: After the Empress Dowager Xingsheng had received her honorific title, court officials requested a general amnesty on that occasion. Mingshan said: 'Frequent amnesties are not the blessing of good people; pardoning offenses may suffice.'
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Dowager Xingsheng received her honorific title, court officials asked for a general amnesty on the occasion. Mingshan said, 'Frequent amnesties do not benefit the virtuous; pardoning offenses is enough.'

sentences.zh: 奉旨出賑山東、河南飢，時彭城、下邳諸州連數十驛，民餓馬斃，而官無文書賑貸，明善以鈔萬二千錠分給之，曰：「擅命獲罪，所不辭也。」

translations.literal: He was ordered to go out and relieve famine in Shandong and Henan. At that time Pengcheng, Xiapi, and other prefectures had relay stations strung together for dozens of posts; the people starved and horses died, yet the government had no documents to authorize famine relief. Mingshan distributed twelve thousand bars of paper money among them, saying: 'If exceeding authority brings guilt, I do not refuse it.'
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to relieve famine in Shandong and Henan. Along dozens of relay stations in Pengcheng, Xiapi, and other prefectures, people starved and horses died, yet officials had no authorization to distribute relief. Mingshan divided twelve thousand bars of paper money among them, saying, 'If exceeding my orders brings punishment, I accept it willingly.'

sentences.zh: 還，修《武宗實錄》，又升翰林侍講學士，預議科舉、服色等事。

translations.literal: On his return he compiled the Veritable Records of Emperor Wuzong, and was again promoted to Hanlin Academician-Expounder, participating in deliberation on the civil service examinations, court dress colors, and related matters.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he compiled the Veritable Records of Emperor Wuzong and was promoted to Hanlin Academician-Expounder, taking part in deliberations on the civil service examinations, court dress, and related matters.

sentences.zh: 延祐二年，始會試天下進士，明善首充考試官，及廷試，又為讀卷官，所取士後多為名臣。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yanyou the first metropolitan examination of scholars empire-wide was held; Mingshan first served as examiner, and at the palace examination was also reader of examination papers. Many of the scholars he selected later became eminent ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yanyou the empire held its first metropolitan examination; Mingshan served as chief examiner and, at the palace examination, as reader of papers. Many of the scholars he selected later became famous ministers.

sentences.zh: 改禮部尚書，正孔氏宗法，以宣聖五十四世孫思晦襲封衍聖公，事上，制可之。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Rites, rectified the Kong clan's rules of descent, and recommended that the fifty-fourth-generation descendant of the Sage, Simiao, inherit the title Duke who spreads holiness; the memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Minister of Rites, rectified the Kong clan's rules of descent, and recommended that Simiao, fifty-fourth-generation descendant of the Sage, inherit the title Duke who Spreads Holiness; the memorial was approved.

sentences.zh: 擢參議中書省事，旋復入翰林為侍讀，歲中拜湖廣行省參知政事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Administrative Councilor of the Secretariat, but soon returned to the Hanlin Academy as Academician-Reader; within the year he was appointed Vice Governor of the Huguang Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Administrative Councilor of the Secretariat, but soon returned to the Hanlin Academy as Reader; within the year he was appointed Vice Governor of the Huguang Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 又召入集賢為侍讀，議廣廟制。

translations.literal: He was again summoned to the Academy of Assembled Worthies as Reader, to deliberate on expanding temple regulations.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned again to the Academy of Assembled Worthies as Reader to deliberate on expanding temple regulations.

sentences.zh: 升翰林學士，修《仁宗實錄》。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Hanlin Academician and compiled the Veritable Records of Emperor Renzong.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Hanlin Academician and compiled the Veritable Records of Emperor Renzong.

sentences.zh: 英宗親課太室，禮官進祝冊，請署御名，命明善代署者三，眷遇之隆，當時莫並焉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong personally officiated at the Grand Temple, the ritual officials presented the prayer text and requested the imperial signature; the emperor three times ordered Mingshan to sign in his stead—a degree of favor unmatched at the time.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong personally performed rites in the Grand Temple, ritual officials presented the prayer text and asked for the imperial signature; three times the emperor ordered Mingshan to sign in his place—a degree of favor unmatched at the time.

sentences.zh: 至治二年，卒於位。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhizhi he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhizhi he died in office.

sentences.zh: 泰定間，贈資善大夫、河南行省左丞，追封清河郡公，諡曰文敏。

translations.literal: During the Taiding reign he was posthumously granted Grand Master for the Promotion of Goodness and Left Vice Governor of the Henan Branch Secretariat, with posthumous enfeoffment as Duke of Qinghe Commandery and the temple name Wenmin.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taiding reign he was posthumously granted Grand Master for the Promotion of Goodness and Left Vice Governor of the Henan Branch Secretariat, enfeoffed posthumously as Duke of Qinghe Commandery, with the temple name Wenmin.

sentences.zh: 明善早以文章自豪，出入秦、漢間，晚益精詣，有文集行世。

translations.literal: Mingshan early took pride in his writings, ranging through Qin and Han models; in his later years he attained even greater refinement, and a collection of writings circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Mingshan early took pride in his writing, moving between Qin and Han models; in later years he attained even greater refinement, and his collected works circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 初在江西、金陵，每與虞集劇論，以相切劘。

translations.literal: When he was first in Jiangxi and Jinling, he often debated fiercely with Yu Ji, each honing the other.
translations.idiomatic: When he was first in Jiangxi and Jinling, he often debated sharply with Yu Ji, each sharpening the other.

sentences.zh: 明善言：「集治諸經，惟硃子所定者耳，自漢以來先儒所嘗盡心者，考之殊未博。」

translations.literal: Mingshan said: 'Ji studies the Classics only as Zhu Xi defined them; the devoted labor of earlier scholars since Han times has not, upon examination, been sufficiently broad.'
translations.idiomatic: Mingshan said, 'Ji studies the Classics only as Zhu Xi defined them; the devoted work of earlier scholars since Han times has not, in his scholarship, been explored nearly enough.'

sentences.zh: 集亦言：「凡為文辭，得所欲言而止，必如明善雲'若雷霆之震驚，鬼神之靈變'然後可，非性情之正也。」

translations.literal: Ji also said: 'In composing literary prose one should say what one intends to say and stop; it must be like Mingshan's "as if thunder's shock and wonder, spirits' mystery and change"—that is not the rectification of one's nature.'
translations.idiomatic: Ji also said, 'In writing prose one should say what one means and stop; it need not be like Mingshan's "like thunder's shock or spirits' transformations"—that is not the true expression of one's nature.'

sentences.zh: 二人初相得甚歡，至京師，乃復不能相下。

translations.literal: The two were at first very pleased with each other; upon reaching the capital they could no longer yield to one another.
translations.idiomatic: At first the two were very fond of each other; once they reached the capital they could no longer get along.

sentences.zh: 董士選之自中台行省江浙也，二人者俱送出都門外，士選曰：「伯生以教導為職，當早還，復初宜更送我。」

translations.literal: When Dong Shixuan was departing from the Central Branch Secretariat for Jiang-Zhe, both men saw him off beyond the city gate. Shixuan said: 'Bosheng's duty is instruction—he ought to return early; Fuchu should escort me further.'
translations.idiomatic: When Dong Shixuan left the Central Secretariat for Jiang-Zhe, both men saw him off beyond the city gate. Shixuan said, 'Bosheng's duty is teaching—he should return early; Fuchu should escort me farther.'

sentences.zh: 集還，明善送至二十里外，士選下馬入邸舍中，為席，出橐中餚，酌酒同飲，乃舉酒屬明善曰：「士選以功臣子，出入台省，無補國家，惟求得佳士數人，為朝廷用之，如復初與伯生，他日必皆光顯，然恐不免為人構間。

translations.literal: Ji returned; Mingshan escorted him twenty li beyond. Shixuan dismounted and entered his lodge, spread a mat, took provisions from his bag, poured wine and drank together, then raised his cup to Mingshan: 'Shixuan, as son of a meritorious minister, has passed in and out of the censorate and secretariat without benefit to the state, only wishing to obtain a few excellent men for the court to employ—such as Fuchu and Bosheng, who one day must all shine brilliantly, yet I fear you will not escape being set at odds by others.
translations.idiomatic: Ji returned; Mingshan escorted Shixuan twenty li farther. Shixuan dismounted at his lodge, spread a mat, took food from his bag, poured wine, and drank with Mingshan. Raising his cup he said, 'As son of a meritorious minister I have moved through the censorate and secretariat without serving the state, only hoping to find a few excellent men for the court—such as you and Bosheng, who will surely rise to eminence, yet I fear others will set you against each other.

sentences.zh: 復初中原人也，仕必當道；

translations.literal: Fuchu is a man of the Central Plains; in office he will surely hold the path of power;
translations.idiomatic: Fuchu is a man of the Central Plains and in office will surely hold power;

sentences.zh: 伯生南人，將為復初摧折。

translations.literal: Bosheng is a Southerner, and will break Fuchu down.
translations.idiomatic: Bosheng is a Southerner and will try to bring Fuchu down.

sentences.zh: 今為我飲此酒，慎勿如是。」

translations.literal: Now drink this wine for me, and take care never to do so.'
translations.idiomatic: Drink this wine for me now, and take care never to let that happen.'

sentences.zh: 明善受巵酒，跪而釂之。

translations.literal: Mingshan received the cup, knelt, and drained it.
translations.idiomatic: Mingshan took the cup, knelt, and drank it down.

sentences.zh: 起立，言曰：「誠如公言，無論他日，今隙已開矣。

translations.literal: Standing he said: 'Truly as you say—but never mind other days; the rift is already open today.
translations.idiomatic: He stood and said, 'What you say is true—but never mind the future; the rift is already open today.

sentences.zh: 請公再賜一卮，明善終身不敢忘公言！」

translations.literal: Please grant me another cup; Mingshan will never in life forget your words!'
translations.idiomatic: Please give me another cup—I will never forget your words as long as I live!'

sentences.zh: 乃再飲而別。

translations.literal: They drank again and parted.
translations.idiomatic: They drank again and parted.

sentences.zh: 真人吳全節，與明善交尤密，嘗求明善作文。

translations.literal: The Perfected Man Wu Quanjie was especially intimate with Mingshan and once asked him to write a piece.
translations.idiomatic: The Daoist adept Wu Quanjie was especially close to Mingshan and once asked him for an essay.

sentences.zh: 既成，明善謂全節曰：「伯生見吾文，必有譏彈，吾所欲知。

translations.literal: When it was done Mingshan told Quanjie: 'When Bosheng sees my essay he is sure to criticize it—that is what I wish to know.
translations.idiomatic: When it was finished Mingshan told Quanjie, 'When Bosheng sees my essay he is sure to criticize it—that is what I want to know.

sentences.zh: 成季為我治具，招伯生來觀之，若已入石，則無及矣。」

translations.literal: Cheng Ji, prepare a feast for me and invite Bosheng to view it; if it has already been carved in stone there will be no remedy.'
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Ji, prepare a feast and invite Bosheng to read it; if it is already carved in stone, nothing can be done.'

sentences.zh: 明日，集至，明善出其文，問何如，集曰：「公能從集言，去百有餘字，則可傳矣。」

translations.literal: The next day Ji arrived. Mingshan produced his essay and asked how it was. Ji said: 'Sir, if you will follow Ji's words and remove a hundred-odd characters, it can be transmitted.'
translations.idiomatic: The next day Ji came. Mingshan showed him the essay and asked his opinion. Ji said, 'If you follow my advice and cut more than a hundred characters, it will be fit to pass down.'

sentences.zh: 明善即泚筆屬集，凡刪百二十字，而文益精當。

translations.literal: Mingshan immediately dipped his brush and entrusted Ji with it; altogether one hundred twenty characters were deleted, and the essay grew more precise and apt.
translations.idiomatic: Mingshan at once handed Ji the brush; one hundred twenty characters were cut in all, and the essay became sharper and more apt.

sentences.zh: 明善大喜，乃歡好如初。

translations.literal: Mingshan was greatly pleased, and their friendly relations resumed as at first.
translations.idiomatic: Mingshan was delighted, and their friendship was as warm as before.

sentences.zh: 集每見明經之士，亦以明善之言告之。

translations.literal: Whenever Ji met scholars versed in the Classics he also told them Mingshan's words.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Ji met scholars versed in the Classics he also repeated Mingshan's words to them.

sentences.zh: 明善一子，晦，廕受峽州路同知，早卒。

translations.literal: Mingshan had one son, Hui, who inherited appointment as Vice Magistrate of the Xia Prefecture circuit road, and died young.
translations.idiomatic: Mingshan had one son, Hui, who inherited the post of Vice Magistrate of the Xia Prefecture circuit and died young.

sentences.zh: ○虞集 弟槃 範梈

translations.literal: ○ Yu Ji; younger brothers Pan and Fan Zhi
translations.idiomatic: ○ Yu Ji; his younger brothers Pan and Fan Zhi

sentences.zh: 虞集，字伯生，宋丞相允文五世孫也。

translations.literal: Yu Ji, styled Bosheng, was fifth-generation descendant of the Song Chief Councilor Yunwen.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Ji, whose style was Bosheng, was a fifth-generation descendant of the Song Chief Councilor Yu Yunwen.

sentences.zh: 曾祖剛簡，為利州路提刑，有治績。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Gangjian was intendant of criminal justice for Lizhou Circuit and had achievements in governance.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Gangjian served as intendant of criminal justice for Lizhou Circuit and achieved a record of good administration.

sentences.zh: 嘗與臨邛魏了翁，成都范仲黼、李心傳輩，講學蜀東門外，得程、硃氏微旨，著《易詩書論語說》，以發明其義，蜀人師尊之。

translations.literal: He once lectured with Wei Liaoweng of Linqiong, Fan Zhongfu and Li Xinchuan of Chengdu, and others outside the east gate of Shu, grasping the subtle purport of the Cheng and Zhu schools; he wrote Expositions on the Changes, Poetry, Documents, and Analects to elucidate their meaning, and the people of Shu honored him as teacher.
translations.idiomatic: He once studied with Wei Liaoweng of Linqiong, Fan Zhongfu and Li Xinchuan of Chengdu, and others outside the east gate of Shu, grasping the essentials of the Cheng and Zhu schools; he wrote Expositions on the Changes, Poetry, Documents, and Analects to clarify their meaning, and the people of Shu revered him as a teacher.

sentences.zh: 祖珏，知連州，亦以文學知名。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jue was prefect of Lianzhou and was also known for literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jue served as prefect of Lianzhou and was also known for literary learning.

sentences.zh: 父汲，黃岡尉。

translations.literal: His father Ji was assistant magistrate of Huanggang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ji was assistant magistrate of Huanggang.

sentences.zh: 宋亡，僑居臨川崇仁，與吳澄為友，澄稱其文清而醇。

translations.literal: When the Song fell he sojourned in Chongren, Linchuan, befriended Wu Cheng, and Cheng praised his writing as clear and pure.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of the Song he settled in Chongren, Linchuan, befriended Wu Cheng, who praised his writing as clear and refined.

sentences.zh: 嘗再至京師，贖族人被俘者十餘口以歸，由是家益貧。

translations.literal: He twice went to the capital and ransomed more than ten kinsmen taken captive, bringing them home; thereby his family grew poorer still.
translations.idiomatic: He twice went to the capital and ransomed more than ten captured kinsmen, bringing them home; his family grew still poorer as a result.

sentences.zh: 晚稍起家，教授於諸生中，得孛術魯翀、歐陽玄而稱許之，以翰林院編修官致仕。

translations.literal: In his later years he slightly raised the family fortunes, teaching among the students; he obtained Bosul Lu Chong and Ouyang Xuan and praised them, and retired as compiler of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In later years he modestly restored the family's fortunes, teaching students; he discovered Bosul Lu Chong and Ouyang Xuan and praised them, and retired as compiler of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 娶楊氏，國子祭酒文仲女。

translations.literal: He married the Yang clan, daughter of Wenzhong, Director of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: He married a woman of the Yang clan, daughter of Wenzhong, Director of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 咸淳間，文仲守衡，以汲從，未有子，為禱於南嶽。

translations.literal: During the Xianchun era Wenzhong was defending Hengzhou and took Ji with him; they had no son yet and prayed at Mount Heng.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianchun era Wenzhong governed Hengzhou and took Ji with him; they had no son yet and prayed at Mount Heng.

sentences.zh: 集之將生，文仲晨起，衣冠坐而假寐，夢一道士至前，牙兵啟曰：「南嶽真人來見。」

translations.literal: When Ji was about to be born, Wenzhong rose early in the morning, sat in cap and gown feigning sleep, and dreamed a Daoist came before him; a guard announced: 'The Perfected Man of Mount Heng has come to call.'
translations.idiomatic: When Ji was about to be born, Wenzhong rose early, dressed formally, and dozed sitting up; he dreamed a Daoist approached, and a guard announced, 'The Perfected Man of Mount Heng has come to call.'

sentences.zh: 既覺，聞甥館得男，心頗異之。

translations.literal: When he awoke he heard that his nephew's lodge had obtained a son, and his heart was rather struck by wonder.
translations.idiomatic: When he awoke he heard that his nephew's household had a son, and he felt something extraordinary had happened.

sentences.zh: 集三歲即知讀書，歲乙亥，汲挈家趨嶺外，干戈中無書冊可攜，楊氏口授《論語》、《孟子》、《左氏傳》、歐蘇文，聞輒成誦。

translations.literal: Ji at three years already knew how to read. In the year yihai Ji led the family south beyond the ranges; amid warfare no books could be carried, and the Yang clan orally taught the Analects, Mencius, Zuo's Commentary, and the writings of Ouyang and Su—he heard and at once could recite.
translations.idiomatic: Ji could read at three. In the year yihai his father led the family south beyond the ranges; amid warfare they could carry no books, and Lady Yang orally taught the Analects, Mencius, Zuo's Commentary, and the writings of Ouyang Xiu and Su Shi—he memorized them as he heard them.

sentences.zh: 比還長沙，就外傅，始得刻本，則已盡讀諸經，通其大義矣。

translations.literal: When they returned to Changsha he sought an outside tutor and first obtained printed editions; he had already read through all the Classics and grasped their great meaning.
translations.idiomatic: When they returned to Changsha he studied under an outside tutor and first obtained printed editions; he had already read all the Classics and grasped their main meaning.

sentences.zh: 文仲世以《春秋》名家，而族弟參知政事棟，明於性理之學，楊氏在室，即盡通其說，故集與弟槃，皆受業家庭，出則以契家子從吳澄遊，授受具有源委。

translations.literal: Wenzhong's family for generations was famed in the Spring and Autumn Annals, while his clansman the Administrative Councilor Dong was clear in the learning of nature and principle; while still in the women's quarters Lady Yang had fully mastered their doctrines. Thus Ji and his younger brother Pan both received instruction within the family; when they went out they followed Wu Cheng as sons of allied families—the transmission had clear lineage.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhong's family was renowned for the Spring and Autumn Annals for generations, and his clansman the Administrative Councilor Dong was accomplished in Neo-Confucian learning; Lady Yang had mastered these doctrines even before marriage. Thus Ji and his younger brother Pan were both educated at home, and when they went out studied with Wu Cheng as allied-family sons—their learning had a clear lineage.

sentences.zh: 左丞董士選自江西除南行台中丞，延集家塾。

translations.literal: Left Vice Governor Dong Shixuan was transferred from Jiangxi to Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Southern Branch Censorate and invited Ji to his family school.
translations.idiomatic: When Left Vice Governor Dong Shixuan was transferred from Jiangxi to Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Southern Branch Censorate, he invited Ji to his family school.

sentences.zh: 大德初，始至京師。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Dade era he first reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Dade era he first reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 以大臣薦，授大都路儒學教授，雖以訓迪為職，而益自充廣，不少暇佚。

translations.literal: On recommendation of a great minister he was appointed Professor of Confucian Studies for the Dadu Circuit; though his duty was instruction, he further enriched himself without sparing leisure.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended by a senior minister, he was appointed Professor of Confucian Studies for the Dadu Circuit; though his duty was teaching, he continued to broaden his learning without sparing himself leisure.

sentences.zh: 除國子助教，即以師道自任，諸生時其退，每挾策趨門下卒業，他館生多相率詣集請益。

translations.literal: He was appointed Assistant Instructor of the Imperial University and at once took the teacher's way upon himself; students timed his departure, each carrying texts hurrying to his gate to complete their studies; students from other lodges often came in groups to Ji seeking further instruction.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Assistant Instructor of the Imperial University and at once took the teacher's role seriously; students timed his departures and hurried to his door with their texts to finish their studies, and students from other lodges often came in groups to seek his instruction.

sentences.zh: 丁內艱，服除，再為助教，除博士。

translations.literal: He mourned his mother's death; when mourning ended he again served as Assistant Instructor and was appointed Erudite.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his mother he again served as Assistant Instructor and was appointed Erudite.

sentences.zh: 監祭殿上，有劉生者，被酒失禮俎豆間，集言諸監，請削其籍。

translations.literal: Supervising sacrifice in the hall, there was a student Liu who, having drunk wine, lost propriety among the sacrificial vessels; Ji reported to the supervisors and requested that his name be struck from the register.
translations.idiomatic: While supervising sacrifice in the hall, a student named Liu, drunk, breached ritual propriety among the sacrificial vessels; Ji reported to the supervisors and asked that Liu be struck from the register.

sentences.zh: 大臣有為劉生謝者，集持不可，曰：「國學，禮義之所出也，此而不治，何以為教！」

translations.literal: A great minister interceded for student Liu, but Ji held firm and would not agree, saying: 'The Imperial University is where ritual and righteousness issue forth—if this is not corrected, how can there be teaching!'
translations.idiomatic: A senior minister interceded for Liu, but Ji refused, saying, 'The Imperial University is where ritual and righteousness originate—if this is not corrected, how can we teach?'

sentences.zh: 仁宗在東宮，傳旨諭集，勿竟其事，集以劉生失禮狀上之，移詹事院，竟黜劉生，仁宗更以集為賢。

translations.literal: The Renzong Emperor, then heir apparent, sent an order telling Ji not to pursue the matter to the end; Ji submitted the record of Liu's breach of ritual, transferred the case to the Household of the Heir Apparent, and in the end dismissed Liu. The heir apparent came to regard Ji as even more worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong, then heir apparent, sent word telling Ji not to pursue the matter; Ji submitted the record of Liu's breach of ritual, transferred the case to the Household of the Heir Apparent, and Liu was dismissed in the end. The heir apparent came to regard Ji as even more worthy.

sentences.zh: 大成殿新賜登歌樂，其師世居江南，樂生皆河北田里之人，情性不相能，集親教之，然後成曲。

translations.literal: The Hall of Great Completion had newly been granted ascending-song music; its master for generations dwelt south of the Yangtze, while the musicians were all village men of Hebei north of the river—their temperaments could not accord. Ji personally taught them, and only then was the melody completed.
translations.idiomatic: The Hall of Great Completion had newly been granted ascending-song music; its master came from families long settled south of the Yangtze, while the musicians were village men from Hebei—their temperaments clashed. Ji taught them personally, and only then was the melody completed.

sentences.zh: 復請設司樂一人掌之，以俟考正。

translations.literal: He again requested that one Director of Music be established to oversee it, pending examination and correction.
translations.idiomatic: He also requested that a Director of Music be appointed to oversee it pending further review.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，責成監學，拜台臣為祭酒，除吳澄司業，皆欲有所更張，以副帝意，集力贊其說。

translations.literal: When Renzong acceded he charged the supervisors of study, appointed a censorial minister as Chancellor of the University, and made Wu Cheng Vice Chancellor—all wishing to make reforms to fulfill the emperor's intent; Ji strongly supported their proposals.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong took the throne he charged the university supervisors, appointed a censorial minister as Chancellor, and made Wu Cheng Vice Chancellor—all intending reforms to fulfill the emperor's wishes; Ji strongly supported them.

sentences.zh: 有為異論以沮之者，澄投檄去，集亦以病免。

translations.literal: Some raised contrary opinions to obstruct them; Cheng submitted his resignation and left, and Ji also resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Opponents raised objections; Cheng submitted his resignation and left, and Ji also resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 未幾，除太常博士，丞相拜住方為其院使，間從集問禮器祭義甚悉，集為言先王制作，以及古今因革治亂之由，拜住嘆息，益信儒者有用。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; the Chief Councilor Bayiju was then director of that court and from time to time asked Ji about ritual vessels and sacrificial meaning in great detail. Ji spoke of the former kings' institutions and the causes of change and stability, order and disorder through past and present; Bayiju sighed and came to believe even more that Confucian scholars were useful.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; Chief Councilor Bayiju was then its director and often asked Ji detailed questions about ritual vessels and sacrificial meaning. Ji explained the institutions of the ancient kings and the causes of change and stability through history; Bayiju sighed and came to believe Confucian scholars were truly useful.

sentences.zh: 朝廷方以科舉取士，說者謂治平可力致，集獨以謂當治其源。

translations.literal: The court was just then selecting scholars through the civil service examinations; advocates said good governance could be vigorously attained; Ji alone held that one must rectify the source.
translations.idiomatic: The court was selecting officials through the civil service examinations; advocates said good governance could be achieved quickly; Ji alone held that the source must be addressed first.

sentences.zh: 遷集賢修撰。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Compiler of the Academy of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Compiler of the Academy of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 因會議學校，乃上議曰：「師道立則善人多，學校者，士之所受教，以至於成德達材者也。

translations.literal: Because of deliberations on schools he submitted a memorial saying: 'When the teacher's way is established, good men will be many. Schools are where scholars receive instruction until they complete virtue and realize talent.
translations.idiomatic: During deliberations on schools he submitted a memorial: 'When the teacher's way is established, good men multiply. Schools are where scholars are taught until they complete their virtue and realize their talent.

sentences.zh: 今天下學官，猥以資格授，強加之諸生之上，而名之曰師爾，有司弗信之，生徒弗信之，於學校無益也。

translations.literal: Today school officials throughout the empire are vulgarly appointed by qualification, forcibly set above the students and called teachers—yet the authorities do not trust them, nor do the students trust them; this benefits the schools in nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Today school officials empire-wide are appointed merely by qualification, forced upon students and called teachers—yet officials do not trust them and students do not trust them; this does the schools no good.

sentences.zh: 如此而望師道之立，可乎？

translations.literal: With this, can one hope for the teacher's way to be established?
translations.idiomatic: Can one hope to establish the teacher's way under such conditions?

sentences.zh: 下州小邑之士，無所見聞，父兄所以導其子弟，初無必為學問之實意，師友之游從，亦莫辨其邪正，然則所謂賢材者，非自天降地出，安有可望之理哉！

translations.literal: Scholars of lower prefectures and small districts have nothing to see or hear; fathers and elder brothers in guiding their sons and younger brothers at first have no true intent to pursue learning; in the company of teachers and friends they also cannot distinguish what is heterodox from what is orthodox—then how can the so-called worthy talents descend from heaven or spring from earth? How could there be any ground for hope!
translations.idiomatic: Scholars in remote prefectures and small towns have little to see or hear; fathers and elder brothers guide their sons without genuine intent to pursue learning; among teachers and friends they cannot distinguish orthodoxy from heterodoxy—then how can worthy talent descend from heaven or spring from earth? What reason is there to expect it?

sentences.zh: 為今之計，莫若使守令求經明行修成德者，身師尊之，至誠懇惻以求之，其德化之及，庶乎有所觀感也。

translations.literal: For the present plan, nothing is better than having prefects and magistrates seek men clear in the Classics and correct in conduct who have completed virtue, personally honor them as teachers, and seek them with utmost sincerity and earnestness—when their moral transformation reaches others, perhaps there will be something to move and inspire.
translations.idiomatic: For the present, prefects and magistrates should seek men accomplished in the Classics and upright in conduct who have completed their virtue, honor them personally as teachers, and seek them with utmost sincerity—when their moral influence spreads, others may be moved and inspired.

sentences.zh: 其次則求夫操履近正，而不為詭異駭俗者，確守先儒經義師說，而不敢妄為奇論者，眾所敬服，而非鄉愿之徒者，延致之日，諷誦其書，使學者習之，入耳著心，以正其本，則他日亦當有所發也。

translations.literal: Next, seek those whose conduct is nearly correct and who do not practice the bizarre to shock custom, who firmly uphold the classical meanings and teachers' doctrines of earlier Confucians and dare not rashly advance strange theories, whom the multitude respect and who are not fellows of the village flatterer type—on the days they are invited, have their books recited so learners may study them, entering the ear and fixing in the heart to rectify the root; then one day they too should have something to unfold.
translations.idiomatic: Next, seek those of nearly correct conduct who do not shock custom with the bizarre, who firmly uphold the classical meanings and teachers' doctrines of earlier Confucians and dare not advance reckless theories, whom people respect and who are not mere village flatterers—when invited, have their books recited for students to study until the words enter the ear and fix in the heart, rectifying the foundation; then one day they too may bear fruit.

sentences.zh: 其次則取鄉貢至京師罷歸者，其議論文藝，猶足以聳動其人，非若泛泛莫知根柢者矣。」

translations.literal: Next, take those presented by the districts who came to the capital and returned after failing— their discourse and literary arts can still stir and move people, unlike the vague who know no root or foundation.'
translations.idiomatic: Next, take those who came to the capital on district presentation and returned after failing—their discourse and literary skill can still stir people, unlike those with no solid foundation.'

sentences.zh: 六年，除翰林待制，兼國史院編修官。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed Attendant Draftsman of the Hanlin Academy, concurrently Compiler of the National History Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was appointed Attendant Draftsman of the Hanlin Academy and concurrently Compiler of the National History Office.

sentences.zh: 仁宗嘗對左右歎曰：「儒者皆用矣，惟虞伯生未顯擢爾。」

translations.literal: Renzong once said to those around him with a sigh: 'Confucian scholars have all been employed—only Yu Bosheng has not yet been prominently elevated.'
translations.idiomatic: Renzong once sighed to those around him, 'Confucian scholars have all been employed—only Yu Bosheng has not yet been prominently promoted.'

sentences.zh: 會晏駕，不及用。

translations.literal: It happened that the emperor died suddenly, and there was no time to employ him.
translations.idiomatic: But the emperor died suddenly before he could be promoted.

sentences.zh: 英宗即位，拜住為相，頗超用賢俊，時集以憂還江南，拜住不知也。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong acceded, Bayiju became chief councilor and greatly promoted worthy men beyond their usual ranks; at the time Ji had returned to Jiangnan on account of mourning, and Bayiju did not know this.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong took the throne, Bayiju became chief councilor and promoted many worthy men; Ji had returned to Jiangnan to mourn, and Bayiju did not know where he was.

sentences.zh: 乃言於上，遣使求之於蜀，不見；

translations.literal: He then spoke to the emperor and sent envoys to seek Ji in Shu, but did not find him;
translations.idiomatic: He told the emperor and sent envoys to seek Ji in Shu, but did not find him;

sentences.zh: 求之江西，又不見；

translations.literal: they sought him in Jiangxi and again did not find him;
translations.idiomatic: they sought him in Jiangxi and again did not find him;

sentences.zh: 集方省墓吳中，使至，受命趨朝，則拜住不及見矣。

translations.literal: Ji was just then visiting graves in Wu; when the envoy arrived he received orders and hurried to court, but Bayiju had no time to see him.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was visiting family graves in Wu; when the envoy arrived he obeyed the summons and hurried to court, but Bayiju died before they could meet.

sentences.zh: 泰定初，考試禮部，言於同列曰：「國家科目之法，諸經傳注各有所主者，將以一道德、同風俗，非欲使學者專門擅業，如近代五經學究之固陋也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiding he examined candidates for the Ministry of Rites and said to his colleagues: 'The state's examination regulations, with each classic and commentary having its appointed authority, intend to unify moral teaching and harmonize custom—not to make scholars specialize and monopolize learning, like the narrow pedantry of recent Five Classics pedants.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taiding he served as examiner for the Ministry of Rites and told his colleagues, 'The examination system, with each classic and commentary having its appointed interpretation, aims to unify moral teaching and harmonize custom—not to make scholars specialize narrowly, like the pedantic Five Classics tutors of recent times.

sentences.zh: 聖經深遠​​，非一人之見可盡，試藝之文，推其高者取之，不必先有主意。

translations.literal: The sacred classics are profound and far-reaching; no single person's view can exhaust them. In examination essays, promote the higher ones for selection—there is no need to have a prior fixed opinion.
translations.idiomatic: The sacred classics are profound; no single view can exhaust them. In examination essays, select the best—there is no need to decide in advance.

sentences.zh: 若先定主意，則求賢之心狹，而差自此始矣。」

translations.literal: If one fixes an opinion beforehand, the mind in seeking worthies grows narrow, and error begins from this.'
translations.idiomatic: If examiners fix their opinions beforehand, the search for talent narrows, and error begins there.'

sentences.zh: 後再為考官，率持是說，故所取每稱得人。

translations.literal: Later, when he again served as examiner, he generally held to this doctrine, and therefore those he selected were each praised as the right men.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when he again served as examiner, he generally held to this view, and those he selected were praised as the right men.

sentences.zh: 泰定初，除國子司業，遷秘書少監。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiding he was appointed Vice Chancellor of the Imperial University and transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taiding he was appointed Vice Chancellor of the Imperial University and then Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 天子幸上都，以講臣多高年，命集與集賢侍讀學士王結執經以從，自是歲嘗在行。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven visited the Upper Capital, because many lecturing ministers were advanced in years, he ordered Ji and Wang Jie, Reader of the Academy of Assembled Worthies, to hold the classics and accompany him; from then on they annually traveled with the court.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited the Upper Capital, many lecturing ministers being elderly, he ordered Ji and Wang Jie, Reader of the Academy of Assembled Worthies, to hold the classics and accompany him; thereafter they traveled with the court each year.

sentences.zh: 經筵之制，取經史中切於心德治道者，用國語、漢文兩進讀，潤譯之際，患夫陳聖學者未易於盡其要，指時務者尤難於極其情，每選一時精於其學者為之，猶數日乃成一篇，集為反覆古今名物之辨以通之，然後得以無忤，其辭之所達，萬不及一，則未嘗不退而竊嘆焉。

translations.literal: The classic lecture system selected from the classics and histories passages bearing on inner virtue and governance, reading them in both the national language and Chinese. In polishing and translating, the difficulty was that those expounding sage learning could not easily exhaust the essentials, while those addressing current affairs found it especially hard to reach the full truth of the matter. Each time they chose one scholar accomplished in the subject for the task, yet several days were still needed to complete one piece. Ji would repeatedly clarify distinctions of names and things past and present to make them coherent, and only then could they be without offense—but of what the words conveyed, not one in ten thousand was reached, and he never failed to withdraw and sigh in private.
translations.idiomatic: The classic lecture system drew from the classics and histories passages relevant to moral cultivation and governance, read in both Mongolian and Chinese. In polishing the translations, those expounding sage learning could not easily convey the essentials, and those addressing current affairs found it especially hard to capture the full truth. Each time they chose one expert scholar, yet several days were still needed for one piece. Ji would clarify distinctions of names and things past and present until the text cohered—but of what the words truly conveyed, scarcely a fraction came through, and he would withdraw and sigh in private.

sentences.zh: 拜翰林直學士，俄兼國子祭酒。

translations.literal: He was appointed Direct Academician of the Hanlin Academy and soon also Chancellor of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Direct Academician of the Hanlin Academy and soon also Chancellor of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 嘗因講罷，論京師恃東南運糧為實，竭民力以航不測，非所以寬遠人而因地利也。

translations.literal: Once after a lecture he discussed how the capital relied on grain transport from the southeast as its substance, exhausting the people's strength to sail uncertain seas—this was not the way to ease distant peoples and follow local advantage.
translations.idiomatic: Once after a lecture he argued that the capital's reliance on grain transport from the southeast exhausted the people's strength on uncertain seas—not the way to ease distant regions and use local resources.

sentences.zh: 與同列進曰：「京師之東，瀕海數千里，北極遼海，南濱青、齊，萑葦之場也，海潮日至，淤為沃壤，用浙人之法，築堤捍水為田，聽富民欲得官者，合其眾分授以地，官定其畔以為限，能以萬夫耕者，授以萬夫之田，為萬夫之長，千夫、百夫亦如之，察其惰者而易之。

translations.literal: Together with his colleagues he submitted: 'East of the capital, along the sea for several thousand li, reaching Liaodong in the north and Qing and Qi in the south, are fields of reeds and rushes. The sea tide comes daily and silts into fertile soil. Using the Zhe people's method, build dikes to hold back water and make fields. Permit wealthy households who desire office to gather their followers and divide land among them; officials fix the boundaries as limits. Whoever can farm with ten thousand men is granted ten thousand men's fields and made chief of ten thousand men; chiefs of a thousand and a hundred are likewise appointed, and the idle are observed and replaced.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted with his colleagues: 'East of the capital, along thousands of li of coast from Liaodong to Qing and Qi, lie reed marshes where daily tides deposit fertile silt. Using Zhe methods, build dikes to reclaim fields. Let wealthy men who seek office gather followers and divide land among them, with officials fixing boundaries. Whoever farms with ten thousand men receives that much land and becomes chief of ten thousand; chiefs of a thousand and a hundred are appointed likewise, and the idle are replaced.

sentences.zh: 一年，勿徵也；

translations.literal: For one year, do not levy taxes;
translations.idiomatic: For the first year, levy no taxes;

sentences.zh: 二年，勿徵也；

translations.literal: for two years, do not levy;
translations.idiomatic: for the second year, levy none;

sentences.zh: 三​​年，視其成，以地之高下，定額於朝廷，以次漸征之；

translations.literal: in the third year, observe the yield, fix quotas for the court according to the land's elevation, and levy gradually in sequence;
translations.idiomatic: in the third year, assess the yield, fix quotas for the court by land quality, and levy taxes gradually;

sentences.zh: 五年，有積蓄，命以官，就所儲給以祿；

translations.literal: in the fifth year, when there is accumulation, appoint to office and grant salary from what is stored;
translations.idiomatic: in the fifth year, when stores accumulate, grant office and pay salaries from the harvest;

sentences.zh: 十年，佩之符印，得以傳子孫，如軍官之法。

translations.literal: in the tenth year, bestow tally and seal, permitting transmission to sons and grandsons, as with military officers.
translations.idiomatic: in the tenth year, grant tally and seal, heritable by sons and grandsons, as with military officers.

sentences.zh: 則東面民兵數萬，可以近衞京師，外禦島夷；

translations.literal: Then tens of thousands of militia on the eastern side can guard the capital at close hand and defend outward against island barbarians;
translations.idiomatic: Then tens of thousands of eastern militia could guard the capital nearby and defend against island raiders;

sentences.zh: 遠寬東南海運，以紓疲民；

translations.literal: greatly ease the southeast sea transport and relieve the exhausted people;
translations.idiomatic: greatly ease southeast sea transport and relieve the exhausted populace;

sentences.zh: 遂富民得官之志，而獲其用；

translations.literal: thereby fulfill wealthy men's desire for office and gain their service;
translations.idiomatic: thereby fulfill wealthy men's desire for office and gain their service;

sentences.zh: 江海遊食盜賊之類，皆有所歸。」

translations.literal: and the wandering eaters, thieves, and such of rivers and seas will all have somewhere to belong.'
translations.idiomatic: and wandering laborers, thieves, and such of rivers and seas would all have a place to settle.'

sentences.zh: 議定於中，說者以為一有此制，則執事者必以賄成，而不可為矣。

translations.literal: The plan was settled in the center, but advocates said that once this system existed, those in charge would surely complete it through bribes, and it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was settled at court, but critics said that once this system existed, officials would surely complete it through bribes, and it could not be done.

sentences.zh: 事遂寢。

translations.literal: The matter was then shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was shelved.

sentences.zh: 其后海口萬戶之設，大略宗之。

translations.literal: Later the establishment of the Haikou myriarchate followed this in broad outline.
translations.idiomatic: Later the establishment of the Haikou myriarchate followed this plan in broad outline.

sentences.zh: 文宗在潛邸，已知集名，既即位，命集仍兼經筵。

translations.literal: When Wenzong was in his hidden residence he already knew Ji's name; once he acceded he ordered Ji to continue concurrently in the classic lectures.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenzong was still heir apparent he already knew Ji's reputation; once enthroned he ordered Ji to continue in the classic lectures.

sentences.zh: 嘗以先世墳墓在吳、越者，歲久湮沒，乞一郡自便，帝曰；

translations.literal: Once, because ancestral graves in Wu and Yue had long been submerged, he begged for a prefecture where he might be at ease. The emperor said:
translations.idiomatic: Once, because ancestral graves in Wu and Yue had long been lost, he asked for a prefecture for his convenience. The emperor said:

sentences.zh: 「爾材何不堪，顧今未可去爾。」

translations.literal: 'What office is your talent not fit for? Only that you cannot be let go for now.'
translations.idiomatic: 'What office is beyond your talent? Only that I cannot let you go now.'

sentences.zh: 除奎章閣侍書學士。

translations.literal: He was appointed Academician-Scribe of the Kuizhang Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Academician-Scribe of the Kuizhang Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 時關中大饑，民枕籍而死，有方數百里無孑遺者，帝問集何以救關中，對曰：「承平日久，人情宴安，有誌之士，急於近效，則怨讟興焉。

translations.literal: At the time Guanzhong suffered great famine; the people died lying atop one another, and in places several hundred li square not a soul survived. The emperor asked Ji how to save Guanzhong. He replied: 'After long peace, human feelings grow complacent; men of purpose, eager for immediate results, give rise to resentment and slander.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Guanzhong suffered severe famine; people died piled upon one another, and in places hundreds of li square not a soul survived. The emperor asked how to save Guanzhong. Ji replied, 'After long peace people grow complacent; men of purpose, eager for quick results, provoke resentment and slander.

sentences.zh: 不幸大災之餘，正君子為治作新之機也，若遣一二有仁術、知民事者，稍寬其禁令，使得有所為，隨郡縣擇可用之人，因舊民所在，定城郭，修閭里，治溝洫，限畎畝，薄徵斂，招其傷殘老弱，漸以其力治之，則遠去而來歸者漸至，春耕秋斂，皆有所助，一二歲間，勿徵勿徭，封域既正，友望相濟，四面而至者，均齊方一，截然有法，則三代之民，將見出於空虛之野矣。」

translations.literal: After the misfortune of great disaster, this is precisely the opportunity for gentlemen to renew governance. If one or two men of humane methods who understand the people's affairs are sent, slightly easing prohibitions so they may act, selecting usable men in each prefecture and county, following where the old populace dwells to fix walls and towns, repair neighborhoods, manage ditches and canals, limit fields, lighten levies, and summon the wounded, crippled, old, and weak—gradually governing them with their own strength—then those who fled far will gradually return. Spring plowing and autumn harvest will all receive aid. For a year or two, levy no taxes and impose no corvée. Once the boundaries are set right and mutual aid established, those arriving from all sides will be equalized into one whole with clear law—then the people of the Three Dynasties will be seen emerging from empty wilderness.'
translations.idiomatic: After such disaster, this is precisely when gentlemen may renew governance. Send one or two men skilled in humane administration who understand the people's needs, ease prohibitions slightly so they may act, select capable men in each prefecture and county, resettle people where they once lived, rebuild towns and neighborhoods, repair irrigation, limit fields, lighten taxes, and gather the wounded, elderly, and weak—gradually restoring order with their own labor—then refugees will gradually return. Spring planting and autumn harvest will receive support. For a year or two levy no taxes and impose no corvée. Once boundaries are set and mutual aid established, arrivals from all sides will be organized under clear law—then the people of the Three Dynasties may emerge again from empty wilderness.'

sentences.zh: 帝稱善。

translations.literal: The emperor praised this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised the plan.

sentences.zh: 因進曰：「幸假臣一郡，試以此法行之，三五年間，必有以報朝廷者。」

translations.literal: He then advanced: 'I beg Your Majesty to lend me one prefecture to try this method; within three or five years there will surely be something to report to the court.'
translations.idiomatic: He added, 'Please grant me one prefecture to try this method; within three to five years I will have results to report to the court.'

sentences.zh: 左右有曰：「虞伯生欲以此去爾。」

translations.literal: Those around him said: 'Yu Bosheng wishes to use this to leave you.'
translations.idiomatic: Those around the emperor said, 'Yu Bosheng wants to use this to leave court.'

sentences.zh: 遂罷其議。

translations.literal: The proposal was then dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 有敕諸兼職不過三，免國子祭酒。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that concurrent posts should not exceed three; he was relieved of the Chancellorship of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: An edict limited concurrent posts to three; he was relieved of the Chancellorship of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 時宗籓暌隔，功臣汰侈，政教未立，帝將策士於廷，集被命為讀卷官，乃擬制策以進，首以「勸親親，體群臣，同一風俗，協和萬邦」為問，帝不用。

translations.literal: At the time the imperial clans were estranged, meritorious ministers extravagant, and political teaching not yet established. The emperor was about to examine scholars in court; Ji was ordered as reader of examination papers and drafted the policy questions to submit, taking as the first topic 'Encourage affection among kin, embody the multitude of ministers, unify customs, and harmonize the myriad states'—the emperor did not use them.
translations.idiomatic: At the time imperial clans were estranged, meritorious ministers extravagant, and governance unsettled. The emperor was to examine scholars at court; Ji was appointed reader of papers and drafted policy questions, leading with 'Encourage kinship affection, embody all ministers, unify customs, and harmonize the myriad states'—the emperor did not adopt them.

sentences.zh: 集以入侍燕閒，無益時政，且媢嫉者多，乃與大學士忽都魯都兒迷失等進曰：「陛下出獨見，建奎章閣，覽書籍，置學士員，以備顧問。

translations.literal: Ji held that attending in leisurely banquets brought no benefit to current policy, and moreover many were jealous. He therefore advanced with Grand Academician Qutlugh Durmish and others: 'Your Majesty, acting on unique insight, established the Kuizhang Pavilion, perused books, and placed academicians to serve as advisers.
translations.idiomatic: Ji felt that attending leisurely banquets did not help current policy, and many were jealous of him. He advanced with Grand Academician Qutlugh Durmish and others, 'Your Majesty, acting on your own insight, established the Kuizhang Pavilion, perused books, and placed academicians as advisers.

sentences.zh: 臣等備員，殊無補報，竊恐有累聖德，乞容臣等辭職。」

translations.literal: We fill posts but have in truth no repayment to offer; we fear in private that we burden Your sagely virtue, and beg that you permit us to resign.'
translations.idiomatic: We fill these posts but have nothing to offer in return; we fear we burden Your sagely virtue and beg permission to resign.'

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「昔我祖宗，睿智聰明，其於致理之道，生而知之，朕早歲跋涉難阻，視我祖宗，既乏生知之明，於國家治體，豈能周知？

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'In former days my ancestors were wise and intelligent; in the way of bringing order they knew it from birth. I in my early years struggled through hardship; compared with my ancestors I lack innate knowing clarity—how could I thoroughly know the state's governing structure?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, 'My ancestors were wise and intelligent and knew governance from birth. I struggled through hardship in my youth; compared with them I lack innate wisdom—how could I thoroughly understand the state's governing structure?

sentences.zh: 故立奎章閣，置學士員，以祖宗明訓、古昔治亂得失，日陳於前，卿等其悉所學，以輔朕志。

translations.literal: Therefore I established the Kuizhang Pavilion and placed academicians, that the ancestors' clear instructions and the gains and losses of order and disorder in antiquity be daily set before me. You must exhaust what you have learned to assist my purpose.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I established the Kuizhang Pavilion and placed academicians, so that the ancestors' clear instructions and the lessons of order and disorder in antiquity are set before me daily. Apply all you have learned to assist my purpose.

sentences.zh: 若軍國機務，自有省院台任之，非卿等責也。

translations.literal: As for military and state affairs, the Secretariat, Censorate, and Bureau have their own charge—this is not your responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Military and state affairs are the responsibility of the Secretariat, Censorate, and Bureau—not yours.

sentences.zh: 其勿復辭。」

translations.literal: Do not resign again.'
translations.idiomatic: Do not resign again.'

sentences.zh: 有旨採輯本朝典故，仿唐、宋《會要》，修《經世大典》，命集與中書平章政事趙世延同任總裁。

translations.literal: An order was issued to gather and compile precedents of the dynasty, following the Tang and Song Institutes, to compile the Great Compendium for Governing the Age; Ji and Administrative Councilor Zhao Shiyan were ordered to serve jointly as chief editors.
translations.idiomatic: An order was issued to gather dynastic precedents, following the Tang and Song Institutes, to compile the Great Compendium for Governing the Age; Ji and Administrative Councilor Zhao Shiyan were appointed joint chief editors.

sentences.zh: 集言：「禮部尚書馬祖常，多聞舊章，國子司業楊宗瑞，素有歷像地理記問度數之學，可共領典；

translations.literal: Ji said: 'Minister of Rites Ma Zuchang is widely versed in old regulations; Vice Chancellor Yang Zongrui of the Imperial University has long possessed learning in calendrical astronomy, geography, records, and measures—they may jointly direct the compilation;
translations.idiomatic: Ji said, 'Minister of Rites Ma Zuchang is widely versed in old regulations; Vice Chancellor Yang Zongrui has long mastered calendrical astronomy, geography, and measures—they may jointly direct the compilation;

sentences.zh: 翰林修撰謝端、應奉蘇天爵、太常李好文、國子助教陳旅、前詹事院照磨宋纟茲、通事舍人王士點，俱有見聞，可助撰錄。

translations.literal: Hanlin Compiler Xie Duan, Attendant Su Tianjue, Court of Imperial Sacrifices Li Haowen, University Assistant Instructor Chen Lü, former Registrar Song Zi of the Household of the Heir Apparent, and Imperial Translator Wang Shidian—all have knowledge and may assist in compilation.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Compiler Xie Duan, Attendant Su Tianjue, Court of Imperial Sacrifices Li Haowen, University Assistant Instructor Chen Lü, former Registrar Song Zi of the Household of the Heir Apparent, and Imperial Translator Wang Shidian—all have relevant knowledge and may assist in compilation.

sentences.zh: 庶幾是書早成。」

translations.literal: Perhaps this book may be completed early.'
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps the work may be completed sooner.'

sentences.zh: 帝以嘗命修遼、金、宋三史，未見成績，《大典》令閣學士專率其屬為之。

translations.literal: The emperor, because he had once ordered compilation of the histories of Liao, Jin, and Song without seeing results, ordered that for the Great Compendium the pavilion academicians alone lead their subordinates in the work.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, having once ordered the histories of Liao, Jin, and Song without results, ordered pavilion academicians alone to lead their staffs on the Great Compendium.

sentences.zh: 既而以累朝故事有未備者，請以翰林國史院修祖宗實錄時百司所具事蹟參訂。

translations.literal: Later, because precedents of successive reigns were incomplete, he requested using the records furnished by the hundred offices when the Hanlin National History Office compiled the ancestors' veritable records for collation.
translations.idiomatic: Later, because precedents of successive reigns were incomplete, he asked to use records furnished by the hundred offices when the Hanlin National History Office compiled the ancestors' veritable records.

sentences.zh: 翰林院臣言於帝曰：「實錄，法不得傳於外，則事蹟亦不當示人。」

translations.literal: Hanlin officials said to the emperor: 'Veritable records by law may not be transmitted outside; then the factual records also ought not be shown to others.'
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin officials told the emperor, 'Veritable records may not by law be transmitted outside; therefore those records should not be shown to others either.'

sentences.zh: 又請以國書《脫卜赤顏》增修太祖以來事蹟，承旨塔失海牙曰：「《脫卜赤顏》非可令外人傳者。」

translations.literal: He also requested using the national book Secret History of the Mongols to augment records from Taizu onward. Academician-in-Chief Tashihaya said: 'The Secret History is not something that may be transmitted to outsiders.'
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to use the national book Secret History of the Mongols to augment records from Taizu onward. Academician-in-Chief Tashihaya said, 'The Secret History may not be transmitted to outsiders.'

sentences.zh: 遂皆已。

translations.literal: Both requests were then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Both requests were denied.

sentences.zh: 俄世延歸，集專領其事，再閱歲，書乃成，凡八百帙。

translations.literal: Before long Shiyan returned home; Ji alone directed the matter, and after two more years the book was completed, altogether eight hundred fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Shiyan returned home; Ji directed the work alone, and after two more years the book was completed—eight hundred fascicles in all.

sentences.zh: 既上進，以目疾丐解職，不允，乃舉治書侍御史馬祖常自代，不報。

translations.literal: After it was submitted he begged release from office on account of eye disease; this was not granted. He then recommended Investigating Censor Ma Zuchang to replace him; no reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: After submission he asked to resign because of eye disease; the request was denied. He recommended Investigating Censor Ma Zuchang to replace him; no reply came.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞趙世安乘間為集請曰：「虞伯生久居京師，甚貧，又病目，幸假一外任，便醫。」

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Zhao Shi'an seized an opportunity to request for Ji: 'Yu Bosheng has long dwelt in the capital, is very poor, and also suffers eye disease; I beg you grant him an outside post for convenient medical treatment.'
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Zhao Shi'an seized an opportunity to request for Ji, 'Yu Bosheng has long lived in the capital, is very poor, and suffers from eye disease; please grant him an outside post for medical treatment.'

sentences.zh: 帝怒曰：「一虞伯生，汝輩不容耶！」

translations.literal: The emperor angrily said: 'One Yu Bosheng—you people cannot tolerate him!'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor angrily said, 'One Yu Bosheng—you people cannot tolerate him!'

sentences.zh: 帝方向用文學，以集弘才博識，無施不宜，一時大典冊咸出其手，故重聽其去。

translations.literal: The emperor was then inclined to employ literary learning; because Ji's great talent and broad knowledge were fit for any application, all great compendia of the time came from his hand—therefore he heavily discounted letting him go.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then inclined to employ literary talent; Ji's great learning fit every need, and all major compendia of the time came from his hand—therefore he would not let him go.

sentences.zh: 集每承詔有所述作，必以帝王之道、治忽之故，從容諷切，冀有感悟，承顧問及古今政治得失，尤委曲盡言，或隨事規諫，出不語人。

translations.literal: Whenever Ji received orders for composition he invariably took the way of emperors and kings and the causes of order and collapse, gently admonishing in hope of awakening understanding. When receiving consultation on the gains and losses of government past and present, he especially spoke with full circumlocution, or admonished according to the matter—yet did not speak of it to others when he left.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Ji received orders to compose, he invariably addressed the way of emperors and kings and the causes of rise and fall, gently admonishing in hope of awakening understanding. When consulted on political gains and losses past and present, he spoke with particular thoroughness, or admonished as occasions arose—yet never spoke of it to others afterward.

sentences.zh: 諫或不入，歸家悒悒不樂。

translations.literal: When admonition was not accepted he returned home displeased and unhappy.
translations.idiomatic: When his admonitions were not heeded he returned home displeased and unhappy.

sentences.zh: 家人見其然，不敢問其故也。

translations.literal: His family, seeing him thus, did not dare ask the reason.
translations.idiomatic: His family, seeing him thus, did not dare ask why.

sentences.zh: 時世家子孫以才名進用者眾，患其知遇日隆，每思有以間之。

translations.literal: At the time many descendants of great families advanced through literary reputation; they resented his daily rising favor and constantly thought how to set him at odds.
translations.idiomatic: At the time many descendants of great families advanced through literary reputation; they resented his rising favor and constantly sought ways to set him at odds.

sentences.zh: 既不效，則相與摘集文辭，指為譏訕，賴天子察知有自，故不能中傷，然集遇其人，未嘗少變。

translations.literal: When this failed they together picked out phrases from Ji's writings and called them satirical; relying on the Son of Heaven's perception that there was cause, they could not wound him—but when Ji met such people he never changed in the least.
translations.idiomatic: When that failed they picked phrases from Ji's writings and called them satirical; the emperor perceived their motive, so they could not harm him—but when Ji met such people he never changed his manner.

sentences.zh: 一日，命集草制封乳母夫為營都王，使貴近阿榮、巎巎傳旨。

translations.literal: One day he ordered Ji to draft an edict enfeoffing the wet-nurse's husband as Prince of Yingdu, sending the intimate favorites Arong and Kuikui to convey the order.
translations.idiomatic: One day he ordered Ji to draft an edict enfeoffing the wet-nurse's husband as Prince of Yingdu, sending the intimate favorites Arong and Kuikui to convey the order.

sentences.zh: 二人者，素忌集，繆言制封營國公，集具藳，俄丞相自榻前來索制詞甚急，集以藳進，丞相愕然問故，集知為所紿，即請易藳以進，終不自言，二人者愧之。

translations.literal: The two had long resented Ji and falsely said the edict enfeoffed him as Duke of Ying State. Ji prepared the draft; soon the chief councilor came from before the couch urgently seeking the edict text. Ji submitted the draft; the councilor was startled and asked the reason. Ji knew he had been deceived and at once requested to change the draft and submit it, but never spoke of it himself. The two were ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: The two had long resented Ji and falsely said the edict made him Duke of Ying State. Ji prepared the draft; soon the chief councilor came urgently from the imperial couch seeking the edict draft. Ji submitted it; the councilor was startled and asked why. Ji knew he had been deceived and at once asked to revise and resubmit the draft, but never spoke of it himself. The two were ashamed.

sentences.zh: 其雅量類如此。

translations.literal: His generous forbearance was generally of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: His generous forbearance was generally of this sort.

sentences.zh: 論薦人材，必先器識，心所未善，不為牢籠以沽譽；

translations.literal: In discussing recommendation of talent he always put capacity and insight first; those not to his mind he would not draw into his net to buy reputation;
translations.idiomatic: In recommending talent he always put capacity and insight first; those not to his liking he would not cultivate for reputation;

sentences.zh: 評議文章，不折之於至當不止，其詭於經者，文雖善，不與也。

translations.literal: in critiquing essays he did not stop until they reached utmost propriety; those heterodox toward the classics, though the writing was good, he would not approve.
translations.idiomatic: in critiquing essays he did not stop until they reached utmost propriety; those heterodox toward the classics, however good the writing, he would not approve.

sentences.zh: 雖以此二者忤物速謗，終不為動。

translations.literal: Though on these two accounts he offended people and quickly drew slander, he was never moved.
translations.idiomatic: Though these two practices offended many and brought quick slander, he was never moved.

sentences.zh: 光人龔伯璲，以才俊為馬祖常所喜，祖常為御史中丞，伯遂遊其門，祖常亟稱之，欲集為薦引，集不可，曰：「是子雖小有才，然非遠器，亦恐不得令終。」

translations.literal: The Guang native Gong Bojun, talented and handsome, was favored by Ma Zuchang. When Zuchang was Censor-in-Chief, Bojun frequented his gate; Zuchang often praised him and wished Ji to recommend him. Ji would not agree, saying: 'This fellow, though he has some small talent, is not material for the long term; I also fear he may not end well.'
translations.idiomatic: The Guang native Gong Bojun, talented and handsome, was favored by Ma Zuchang. When Zuchang was Censor-in-Chief, Bojun frequented his house; Zuchang often praised him and wanted Ji to recommend him. Ji refused, saying, 'This man has some talent, but lacks long-term capacity; I fear he may not end well.'

sentences.zh: 祖常猶未以為然。

translations.literal: Zuchang still did not consider this correct.
translations.idiomatic: Zuchang still did not agree.

sentences.zh: 一日，邀集過其家，設宴，酒半，出薦牘求集署，集固拒之，祖常不樂而罷。

translations.literal: One day he invited Ji to his home, set a banquet, and when the wine was half gone produced a recommendation document asking Ji to sign. Ji firmly refused; Zuchang ended the feast displeased.
translations.idiomatic: One day he invited Ji to his home and held a banquet; halfway through the wine he produced a recommendation document asking Ji to sign. Ji firmly refused; Zuchang ended the feast displeased.

sentences.zh: 文宗崩，集在告，欲謀南還，弗果。

translations.literal: When Wenzong died Ji was on leave and wished to plan a return south; he did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenzong died Ji was on leave and wished to return south; he did not succeed.

sentences.zh: 幼君崩，大臣將立妥歡帖穆爾太子，用至大故事，召諸老臣赴上都議政，集在召列。

translations.literal: When the young ruler died the great ministers were about to establish Toghon Temür as heir apparent; following the Zhida precedent they summoned old ministers to the Upper Capital to deliberate on government—Ji was among those summoned.
translations.idiomatic: When the young emperor died the great ministers were about to establish Toghon Temür as heir apparent; following the Zhida precedent they summoned senior ministers to the Upper Capital to deliberate—Ji was among those summoned.

sentences.zh: 祖常使人告之曰：「御史有言。」

translations.literal: Zuchang sent someone to tell him: 'The censorate has something to say.'
translations.idiomatic: Zuchang sent someone to tell him, 'The censorate has something to say.'

sentences.zh: 乃謝病歸臨川。

translations.literal: He then pleaded illness and returned to Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: He then pleaded illness and returned to Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 初，文宗在上都，將立其子阿剌忒納答剌為皇太子，乃以妥歡帖穆爾太子乳母夫言，明宗在日，素謂太子非其子，黜之江南，驛召翰林學士承旨阿鄰帖木兒、奎章閣大學士忽都魯篤彌實書其事於《脫卜赤顏》，又召集使書詔，播告中外。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Wenzong was at the Upper Capital about to establish his son Aratnadara as crown prince, he relied on the wet-nurse's husband of heir apparent Toghon Temür, who said that while Emperor Mingzong lived he had always held the heir was not his son and demoted him to Jiangnan. By relay post he summoned Hanlin Academician-in-Chief Arintemür and Grand Academician Qutlugh Dormish to record the matter in the Secret History, and also summoned the envoy to write the edict and proclaim it within and without.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Wenzong was at the Upper Capital about to establish his son Aratnadara as crown prince, he relied on Toghon Temür's wet-nurse's husband, who said that Mingzong had always held the heir was not his son and demoted him to Jiangnan. By relay post he summoned Hanlin Academician-in-Chief Arintemür and Grand Academician Qutlugh Dormish to record the matter in the Secret History, and summoned an envoy to write the edict and proclaim it throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 時省台諸臣，皆文宗素所信用、同功一體之人，御史亦不敢斥言其事，意在諷集速去而已。

translations.literal: At the time the ministers of the Secretariat and Censorate were all men Wenzong had long trusted and who shared one body in merit; the censorate also did not dare speak bluntly of the matter—the intent was only to hint that Ji should leave quickly.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Secretariat and Censorate ministers were all men Wenzong had long trusted; the censorate also did not dare speak bluntly of the matter—the intent was only to hint that Ji should leave quickly.

sentences.zh: 伯璲後以用事敗，殺其身，世乃服集知人。

translations.literal: Later Bojun failed through wielding power and was put to death; the world then acknowledged Ji's knowledge of men.
translations.idiomatic: Later Bojun fell from power and was executed; the world then acknowledged Ji's judgment of character.

sentences.zh: 元統二年，遣使賜上尊酒、金織文錦二，召還禁林，疾作不能行，屢有敕，即家撰文，褒錫勳舊、侍臣。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuantong envoys were sent bestowing finest wine and two bolts of gold-woven brocade, summoning him back to the Forbidden Grove; illness arose and he could not travel. Repeatedly there were edicts ordering him to compose at home, praising meritorious elders and attending ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuantong envoys were sent with finest wine and two bolts of gold-woven brocade, summoning him back to the Forbidden Grove; illness prevented travel. Repeated edicts ordered him to compose at home, praising meritorious elders and attending ministers.

sentences.zh: 有以舊詔為言者，帝不懌曰：「此我家事，豈由彼書生耶！」

translations.literal: When someone spoke of an old edict the emperor displeasedly said: 'This is my family's affair—how could it be for that bookish fellow!'
translations.idiomatic: When someone cited an old edict the emperor displeasedly said, 'This is my family's affair—how could it be for that bookish fellow!'

sentences.zh: 至正八年五月己未，以病卒，年七十有七。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhizheng, on the day jiwei of the fifth month, he died of illness at the age of seventy-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Zhizheng, on the jiwei day of the fifth month, he died of illness at the age of seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 官自將仕郎十二轉為通奉大夫。

translations.literal: In office he rose through twelve steps from Gentleman for Merit to Grand Master for Court Audience.
translations.idiomatic: In office he rose through twelve ranks from Gentleman for Merit to Grand Master for Court Audience.

sentences.zh: 贈江西行中書省參知政事、護軍，封仁壽郡公。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Vice Governor of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat and Defender of the Army, enfeoffed as Duke of Renshou Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously granted Vice Governor of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat and Defender of the Army, enfeoffed as Duke of Renshou Commandery.

sentences.zh: 集孝友，方二親以故家令德，中遭亂亡，僑寓下邑，左右承順無違。
