translations.literal: Ji was filial and friendly. When both parents, as a family of old virtue, met mid-course chaos and exile, they sojourned in a small town; he attended them left and right in compliance without offense.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was filial and friendly. When both parents, a family of old virtue, met mid-course chaos and exile, they settled in a small town; he attended them in compliance without offense.

sentences.zh: 弟槃，早卒，教育其孤，無異己子。

translations.literal: His younger brother Pan died early; he educated Pan's orphan no differently from his own sons.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Pan died early; he educated Pan's orphan no differently from his own sons.

sentences.zh: 兄採，以筦庫輸賦京師，虧數千緡，盡力營貸代償之，無難色。

translations.literal: His elder brother Cai, through granary duties paying taxes to the capital, was short several thousand strings of cash; Ji exhausted himself raising loans to repay it for him without showing difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Cai, through granary duties paying taxes to the capital, was short several thousand strings of cash; Ji exhausted himself raising loans to repay it without showing reluctance.

sentences.zh: 撫庶弟，嫁孤妹，具有恩意。

translations.literal: He nurtured a younger half-brother and married off an orphaned sister, showing full kindness.
translations.idiomatic: He nurtured a younger half-brother and married off an orphaned sister with full kindness.

sentences.zh: 山林之士知古學者，必折節下之，接後進，雖少且賤，如敵己。

translations.literal: Scholars in mountains and forests who knew ancient learning—he invariably lowered himself to honor them; receiving juniors, though young and lowly, he treated them as equals.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars in reclusion who knew ancient learning—he invariably honored them; receiving juniors, though young and humble, he treated them as equals.

sentences.zh: 當權門赫奕，未嘗有所附麗。

translations.literal: When powerful houses blazed in splendor he never attached himself to any.
translations.idiomatic: When powerful houses blazed in splendor he never attached himself to any.

sentences.zh: 集議中書，正言讜論，多見容受，屢以片言解疑誤，出人於濱死，亦不以為德。

translations.literal: When Ji deliberated at the Secretariat his upright words and loyal opinions were often accepted; he repeatedly with a single phrase resolved doubts and errors, saving people from the brink of death, yet did not regard this as merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Ji deliberated at the Secretariat his upright counsel was often accepted; he repeatedly resolved doubts with a single phrase and saved people from the brink of death, yet did not regard this as merit.

sentences.zh: 張珪、趙世延尤敬禮之，有所疑必諮焉。

translations.literal: Zhang Gui and Zhao Shiyan especially honored him; whenever they had doubts they invariably consulted him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gui and Zhao Shiyan especially honored him; whenever they had doubts they consulted him.

sentences.zh: 家素貧，歸老後食指益眾，登門之士相望於道，好事爭起邸舍以待之。

translations.literal: His family was always poor; after returning in old age mouths to feed grew ever more numerous; scholars calling at his door stretched along the road, and enthusiasts vied to erect lodges to await him.
translations.idiomatic: His family was always poor; after retiring mouths to feed grew ever more numerous; scholars calling at his door stretched along the road, and enthusiasts vied to erect lodges to receive him.

sentences.zh: 然碑板之文，未嘗苟作。

translations.literal: Yet he never carelessly composed inscription texts for steles and boards.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he never carelessly composed stele inscriptions.

sentences.zh: 南昌富民有伍真父者，貲產甲一方，娶諸王女為妻，充本位下郡總管。

translations.literal: Among Nanchang's wealthy was Wu Zhenfu, whose assets ranked first in the region; he married a princess's daughter as wife and served as circuit prefect under his princely house.
translations.idiomatic: Among Nanchang's wealthy was Wu Zhenfu, whose assets ranked first in the region; he married a princess's daughter and served as circuit prefect under his princely house.

sentences.zh: 既卒，其子屬豐城士甘愨求集文銘父墓，奉中統鈔五百錠準禮物，集不許，愨愧嘆而去。

translations.literal: After he died his son entrusted the Fengcheng scholar Gan Que to seek Ji's writing to inscribe his father's tomb, presenting five hundred bars of Zhongtong paper money as customary gift. Ji would not agree; Que left in shame and sighing.
translations.idiomatic: After he died his son asked the Fengcheng scholar Gan Que to seek Ji's writing for his father's tomb inscription, presenting five hundred bars of Zhongtong paper money as customary gift. Ji refused; Que left in shame and sighing.

sentences.zh: 其束脩羔雁之入，還以為賓客費，雖空乏弗卹也。

translations.literal: The dried meat and goose he received as teacher's gifts he returned for guest expenses; though empty and wanting he did not stint.
translations.idiomatic: Teacher's gifts he received he spent on entertaining guests; though impoverished he did not stint.

sentences.zh: 集學雖博洽，而究極本原，研精探微，心解神契，其經緯彌綸之妙，一寓諸文，藹然慶曆乾淳風烈。

translations.literal: Ji's learning, though broad and comprehensive, pursued ultimate origins, refined and probed the subtle, with mind understanding and spirit in accord; the subtlety of his weaving and encompassing was all lodged in his writings, gently redolent of the Qingli and Chunxi style.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's learning, though broad, pursued ultimate origins and probed the subtle with mind and spirit in accord; the subtlety of his comprehensive vision lodged entirely in his writings, gently redolent of the Qingli and Chunxi style.

sentences.zh: 嘗以江左先賢甚眾，其人皆未易知，其學皆未易言，後生晚進知者鮮矣，欲取太原元好問《中州集》遺意，別為《南州集》以表章之，以病目而止。

translations.literal: He once held that worthy men of the Jiangzuo region were very numerous—their persons not easy to know, their learning not easy to speak of—and that later generations knew few of them. He wished to take the intent of Yuan Haowen's Central Plains Collection from Taiyuan and separately compile a Southern Regions Collection to give them expression, but stopped because of eye disease.
translations.idiomatic: He once held that worthy men of the Jiangzuo region were numerous—their persons hard to know, their learning hard to describe—and that later generations knew few of them. He wished to follow Yuan Haowen's Central Plains Collection and compile a Southern Regions Collection to honor them, but stopped because of eye disease.

sentences.zh: 平生為文萬篇，稿存者十二三。

translations.literal: In life he wrote ten thousand pieces; drafts surviving are one or two in ten.
translations.idiomatic: In life he wrote ten thousand pieces; only one or two in ten of his drafts survive.

sentences.zh: 早歲與弟槃同辟書舍為二室，左室書陶淵明詩於壁，題曰陶庵，右室書邵堯夫詩，題曰邵庵​​，故世稱邵庵先生。

translations.literal: In his early years he and his younger brother Pan together opened a study with two rooms; the left room had Tao Yuanming's poetry written on the wall and was titled Tao Hermitage, the right had Shao Yao-fu's poetry and was titled Shao Hermitage—hence the world called him Master of Shao Hermitage.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he and his younger brother Pan built a study with two rooms; the left bore Tao Yuanming's poetry on the wall and was called Tao Hermitage, the right bore Shao Yong's poetry and was called Shao Hermitage—hence the world called him Master of Shao Hermitage.

sentences.zh: 子四人，安民，以廕歷官知吉州路安福州。

translations.literal: He had four sons; Anmin, through hereditary privilege, rose through offices to prefect of Anfu Prefecture in Jizhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons; Anmin, through hereditary privilege, rose to prefect of Anfu Prefecture in Jizhou Circuit.

sentences.zh: 遊其門見稱許者，莆田陳旅，旅亦有文行世。

translations.literal: Among those who studied at his gate and won praise was Chen Lü of Putian; Lü also had literary works circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Among his students who won praise was Chen Lü of Putian, whose writings also circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 國學諸生若蘇天爵、王守誠輩，終身不名他師，皆當世稱名卿者。

translations.literal: University students such as Su Tianjue and Wang Shoucheng never named another teacher all their lives—all were famed ministers of the age.
translations.idiomatic: University students such as Su Tianjue and Wang Shoucheng never acknowledged another teacher all their lives—all became famed ministers of the age.

sentences.zh: 其交遊尤厚者，曰範梈。

translations.literal: Among his especially close friends was Fan Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: His closest friend was Fan Zhi.

sentences.zh: 槃字仲常，延祐五年第進士，授吉安永豐丞。

translations.literal: Pan, styled Zhongchang, passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Yanyou and was appointed assistant magistrate of Yongfeng in Ji'an.
translations.idiomatic: Pan, styled Zhongchang, passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Yanyou and was appointed assistant magistrate of Yongfeng in Ji'an.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂。

translations.literal: He mourned his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: He mourned his father.

sentences.zh: 除湘鄉州判官，頗稱癖古。

translations.literal: He was appointed vice-prefect of Xiangxiang Prefecture and was rather praised as addicted to antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice-prefect of Xiangxiang Prefecture and was known as a lover of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 有富民殺人，使隸己者坐之，上下皆阿從，槃獨不署，殺人者卒不免死，而坐者得以不冤。

translations.literal: A wealthy man committed murder and made his dependent take the blame; above and below all flattered and followed, but Pan alone would not sign. The murderer in the end could not escape death, while the one made to sit escaped being wronged.
translations.idiomatic: A wealthy man committed murder and made his servant take the blame; officials above and below all went along, but Pan alone refused to sign. The murderer was executed in the end, and the scapegoat was spared injustice.

sentences.zh: 有巫至其州，稱神降，告其人曰：「某方火。」

translations.literal: A shaman came to his prefecture, claiming a spirit had descended, and told a man: 'Such-and-such place will burn.'
translations.idiomatic: A shaman came to his prefecture claiming a spirit had descended and told a man, 'Such-and-such place will burn.'

sentences.zh: 即火。

translations.literal: It immediately burned.
translations.idiomatic: It immediately burned.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「明日某方火。」

translations.literal: He again said: 'Tomorrow such-and-such place will burn.'
translations.idiomatic: He said again, 'Tomorrow such-and-such place will burn.'

sentences.zh: 民以火告者，槃皆赴救，至達晝夜，告者數十，寢食盡廢，縣長吏以下皆迎巫至家，厚禮之。

translations.literal: When the people reported fires Pan went to rescue them all, continuing day and night; reporters numbered in the tens and sleep and food were entirely abandoned. County magistrates and below all welcomed the shaman to their homes and honored him lavishly.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever people reported fires Pan rushed to rescue them, continuing day and night; dozens reported and he abandoned sleep and food. County magistrates and below all welcomed the shaman home and honored him lavishly.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「將有大水，且兵至。」

translations.literal: He again said: 'There will be great floodwaters, and troops will arrive.'
translations.idiomatic: He said again, 'There will be great floods, and troops will arrive.'

sentences.zh: 州大家皆盡室逃。

translations.literal: Great families of the prefecture all fled with their entire households.
translations.idiomatic: Great families of the prefecture fled with their entire households.

sentences.zh: 槃得劫火卒一人，訊之，盡得巫黨所為，坐捕盜司。

translations.literal: Pan obtained one soldier who had set fires by robbery; upon interrogation he fully obtained that the shaman's faction had done it, and the case was sent to the Office for Capturing Bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Pan captured a soldier who had set fires by robbery; upon interrogation he learned the shaman's faction was responsible, and the case was sent to the Office for Capturing Bandits.

sentences.zh: 召巫至，鞫之，無敢施鞭棰者，槃謂卒曰：「此將為大亂，安有神乎！」

translations.literal: He summoned the shaman and examined him; none dared apply the whip. Pan told the soldiers: 'This will become great disorder—how could there be spirits!'
translations.idiomatic: He summoned the shaman for examination; none dared apply the whip. Pan told the soldiers, 'This will become great disorder—how could there be spirits!'

sentences.zh: 急治之，盡得黨與數十人，羅絡內外，果將為變者。

translations.literal: He urgently tried the case and fully obtained dozens of accomplices, networked inside and out, who truly were about to make rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: He tried the case urgently and uncovered dozens of accomplices networked inside and out who truly intended rebellion.

sentences.zh: 同僚皆不敢出視，曰：「君自為之。」

translations.literal: Colleagues all did not dare come out to look, saying: 'Sir, handle it yourself.'
translations.idiomatic: Colleagues all refused to get involved, saying, 'Handle it yourself.'

sentences.zh: 槃用斷巫併其黨如法，一時吏民始服儒者為政若此。

translations.literal: Pan sentenced the shaman and his faction together according to law; for a time officials and people first acknowledged that a Confucian could govern thus.
translations.idiomatic: Pan sentenced the shaman and his faction according to law; officials and people then first acknowledged that a Confucian could govern thus.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，除嘉魚縣尹，槃已卒。

translations.literal: When his term ended he was appointed magistrate of Jiayu County, but Pan had already died.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he was appointed magistrate of Jiayu County, but Pan had already died.

sentences.zh: 槃幼時，嘗讀柳子厚《非國語》，以為《國語》誠可非，而柳子之說亦非也，著《非非國語》，時人已歎其有識。

translations.literal: When young Pan once read Liu Zihou's Against the Discourses of the States, holding that the Discourses truly could be criticized, yet Liu's argument was also wrong; he wrote Against Against the Discourses of the States, and people of the time already sighed at his discernment.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Pan read Liu Zongyuan's Against the Discourses of the States, holding that the Discourses could indeed be criticized, yet Liu's argument was also wrong; he wrote Against Against the Discourses of the States, and contemporaries already admired his discernment.

sentences.zh: 《詩》、《書》、《春秋》皆有論著，而《春秋》乃其家學，故尤善。

translations.literal: The Poetry, Documents, and Spring and Autumn Annals all had his treatises; the Spring and Autumn was his family's learning, and therefore he was especially accomplished in it.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote treatises on the Poetry, Documents, and Spring and Autumn Annals; the Spring and Autumn was his family's specialty, and he was especially accomplished in it.

sentences.zh: 讀吳澄所解諸經義，輒得其旨趣所在，澄亟稱之。

translations.literal: Reading Wu Cheng's explications of the classics' meanings, he at once grasped where the purport lay; Cheng frequently praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Reading Wu Cheng's explications of the classics, he at once grasped their purport; Cheng frequently praised him.

sentences.zh: 兄集接方外士，必扣擊其說，嘗以為聖人之教不明，為學者無所底止，苟於吾道異端疑似之間不能深知，而欲竊究夫性命原、死生之故，其不折而歸之者寡矣。

translations.literal: His elder brother Ji received men outside the orthodox fold and invariably probed and tested their doctrines, once holding that the sages' teaching was not clear and scholars had nowhere to rest; if between our Way and heterodoxies seemingly similar one cannot deeply know, yet wishes secretly to investigate the origin of nature and fate and the causes of death and life, few will not break and return.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Ji received men outside the orthodox fold and invariably probed their doctrines, holding that the sages' teaching was unclear and scholars had nowhere to anchor themselves; if one cannot deeply distinguish our Way from similar heterodoxies yet wishes secretly to investigate the origins of nature and fate and the causes of life and death, few will not be led astray.

sentences.zh: 槃不然，聞諸僧在坐，輒不入竟去，其為人方正有如此，雖集亦嚴憚之。

translations.literal: Pan was not so; hearing that monks were seated he would not enter and left straightaway. His uprightness was thus; even Ji strictly feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Pan was not so; hearing monks were present he would not enter and left at once. He was thus upright; even Ji held him in strict regard.

sentences.zh: 然不幸年不及艾而卒。

translations.literal: Yet unhappily he died before reaching fifty.
translations.idiomatic: Yet unhappily he died before reaching fifty.

sentences.zh: 範梈，字亨父，一字德機，清江人。

translations.literal: Fan Zhi, styled Xingfu, with another style Deji, was a man of Qingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhi, styled Xingfu, also known as Deji, came from Qingjiang.

sentences.zh: 家貧，早孤，母熊氏守志不他適，長而教之。

translations.literal: His family was poor; he was orphaned early. His mother, the Xiong clan, kept her resolve and did not marry another; when he grew she taught him.
translations.idiomatic: His family was poor and he was orphaned early. His mother, of the Xiong clan, kept her widowhood and did not remarry; when he grew she taught him.

sentences.zh: 梈天資穎異，所誦讀，輒記憶，雖癯然清寒若不勝衣，於流俗中克自樹立，無苟賤意。

translations.literal: Zhi's native talent was sharp and unusual; whatever he recited and read he at once remembered. Though lean and plainly poor as if unable to bear his clothes, amid vulgar custom he could establish himself without base or servile intent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was extraordinarily quick-witted; whatever he read he remembered at once. Though lean and plainly poor as if his clothes might slip from him, amid vulgar society he held himself upright without base or servile intent.

sentences.zh: 居則固窮守節，竭力以養親，出則假陰陽之技，以給旅食，耽詩工文，用力精深，人罕知者。

translations.literal: At home he held fast in poverty and kept his integrity, exhausting himself to support his parents; abroad he borrowed yin-yang arts to supply travel and food, addicted to poetry and skilled in prose, applying effort with depth and refinement—few knew him.
translations.idiomatic: At home he held fast in poverty and kept his integrity, exhausting himself to support his parents; abroad he used yin-yang arts to earn travel and food, devoted to poetry and skilled in prose with deep refinement—few knew him.

sentences.zh: 年三十六，始客京師，即有聲諸公間，中丞董士選延之家塾。

translations.literal: At thirty-six he first sojourned in the capital and at once had reputation among the great lords; Vice Censor-in-Chief Dong Shixuan invited him to his family school.
translations.idiomatic: At thirty-six he first went to the capital and at once won reputation among senior officials; Vice Censor-in-Chief Dong Shixuan invited him to his family school.

sentences.zh: 以朝臣薦，為翰林院編修官。

translations.literal: On recommendation of a court minister he became compiler of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended by a court minister, he became compiler of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，御史臺擢海南海北道廉訪司照磨，巡歷遐僻，不憚風波瘴癘，所至興學教民，雪理冤滯甚眾。

translations.literal: When his term ended the Censorate promoted him to registrar of the Hainan and Haibei Circuit Integrity Office; touring remote regions he did not fear wind, waves, or miasma. Wherever he arrived he established schools and taught the people, clearing many stuck wrongs.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended the Censorate promoted him to registrar of the Hainan and Haibei Circuit Integrity Office; touring remote regions he did not fear wind, waves, or miasma. Wherever he went he established schools and taught the people, clearing many stuck wrongs.

sentences.zh: 遷江西湖東，長吏素稱嚴明，於僚屬中獨敬異之。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hugan in Jiangxi; the chief official, known for severity and clarity, among subordinates alone honored and regarded him as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Hugan in Jiangxi; the chief official, known for severity, among subordinates alone honored him as extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 選充翰林應奉。

translations.literal: He was selected to serve as Hanlin Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was selected to serve as Hanlin Attendant.

sentences.zh: 御史臺又改擢福建閩海道知事。

translations.literal: The Censorate again transferred and promoted him to Intendant of the Minhai Circuit in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate again promoted him to Intendant of the Minhai Circuit in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 閩俗素污，文繡局取良家子為繡工，無別尤甚，梈作歌詩一篇述其弊，廉訪使取以上聞，皆罷遣之，其弊遂革。

translations.literal: Fujian custom was always corrupt; the Brocade Office took sons of good families as embroiderers, with no distinction—especially severe. Zhi composed a song-poem describing the abuse; the integrity commissioner took it upward to report, and all were dismissed and sent away; the abuse was then reformed.
translations.idiomatic: Fujian custom was corrupt; the Brocade Office took sons of good families as embroiderers without distinction—a severe abuse. Zhi composed a poem describing it; the integrity commissioner reported upward, and all were dismissed; the abuse was reformed.

sentences.zh: 未幾，移疾歸故里。

translations.literal: Before long he pleaded illness and returned to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he pleaded illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 天歷二年，授湖南嶺北道廉訪司經歷，以養親辭。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianli he was appointed administrator of the Hunan and Lingbei Circuit Integrity Office, but declined to support his parents.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianli he was appointed administrator of the Hunan and Lingbei Circuit Integrity Office but declined to care for his parents.

sentences.zh: 是歲，母喪。

translations.literal: That year his mother died.
translations.idiomatic: That year his mother died.

sentences.zh: 明年十月，亦以疾卒，年五十九。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the following year he also died of illness at the age of fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the following year he also died of illness at the age of fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 所著詩文多傳於世。

translations.literal: His poetry and prose mostly circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry and prose circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 梈持身廉正，居官不可干以私，疏食飲水，泊如也。

translations.literal: Zhi maintained himself with integrity and uprightness; in office he could not be approached for private ends; coarse food and water—he was placid thus.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi maintained himself with integrity; in office he could not be approached for private ends; coarse food and water sufficed, and he was placid.

sentences.zh: 吳澄以道學自任，少許可，嘗曰：「若亨父，可謂特立獨行之士矣。」

translations.literal: Wu Cheng took the learning of the Way upon himself and rarely approved anyone; he once said: 'As for Xingfu, he may be called a man who stands alone and acts independently.'
translations.idiomatic: Wu Cheng took Neo-Confucian learning upon himself and rarely approved anyone; he once said, 'Xingfu may be called a man who stands alone and acts independently.'

sentences.zh: 為文志其墓，以東漢諸君子擬之。

translations.literal: He wrote a text for his tomb inscription, comparing him to the gentlemen of the Eastern Han.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote his tomb inscription, comparing him to the gentlemen of the Eastern Han.

sentences.zh: ○揭傒斯

translations.literal: ○ Jie Xisi
translations.idiomatic: ○ Jie Xisi

sentences.zh: 揭傒斯，字曼碩，龍興富州人。

translations.literal: Jie Xisi, styled Manshuo, was a man of Fuzhou in Longxing.
translations.idiomatic: Jie Xisi, whose style was Manshuo, came from Fuzhou in Longxing.

sentences.zh: 父來成，宋鄉貢進士。

translations.literal: His father Laicheng was a Song presenter of tribute from the districts.
translations.idiomatic: His father Laicheng was a Song presenter of tribute from the districts.

sentences.zh: 傒斯幼貧，讀書尤刻苦，晝夜不少懈，父子自為師友，由是貫通百氏，早有文名。

translations.literal: Xisi was poor in youth and read with especial hardship, day and night without slackening; father and son were teacher and friend to each other, thereby penetrating the hundred schools and early gaining literary fame.
translations.idiomatic: Xisi was poor in youth and read with especial diligence, day and night without slackening; father and son were teacher and friend to each other, thereby mastering the hundred schools and gaining literary fame early.

sentences.zh: 大德間，稍出遊湘、漢，湖南帥趙淇，雅號知人，見之驚曰：「他日翰苑名流也。」

translations.literal: During the Dade era he slightly traveled out to Xiang and Han; the Hunan commander Zhao Qi, famed for knowing men, seeing him exclaimed: 'One day a luminary of the Hanlin Grove!'
translations.idiomatic: During the Dade era he traveled to Xiang and Han; Hunan commander Zhao Qi, famed for knowing men, seeing him exclaimed, 'One day a luminary of the Hanlin Grove!'

sentences.zh: 程鉅夫、盧摯，先後為湖南憲長，咸器重之，鉅夫因妻以從妹。

translations.literal: Cheng Jufu and Lu Zhi successively served as Hunan censorial chiefs and all deeply valued him; Jufu gave him his younger cousin in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Jufu and Lu Zhi successively served as Hunan censorial chiefs and all deeply valued him; Jufu gave him his younger cousin in marriage.

sentences.zh: 延祐初，鉅夫、摯列薦於朝，特授翰林國史院編修官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yanyou Jufu and Zhi jointly recommended him to court; he was specially appointed compiler of the Hanlin National History Office.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yanyou Jufu and Zhi jointly recommended him to court; he was specially appointed compiler of the Hanlin National History Office.

sentences.zh: 時平章李孟監修國史，讀其所撰《功臣列傳》，歎曰：「是方可名史筆，若他人，直謄吏牘爾。」

translations.literal: At the time Administrative Councilor Li Meng supervised compilation of the national history; reading Xisi's Biographies of Meritorious Ministers he sighed: 'Only this may be called historian's brushwork; as for others, they merely copy clerks' documents.'
translations.idiomatic: At the time Administrative Councilor Li Meng supervised compilation of the national history; reading Xisi's Biographies of Meritorious Ministers he sighed, 'Only this may be called historian's brushwork; others merely copy clerks' documents.'

sentences.zh: 升應奉翰林文字，仍兼編修，遷國子助教，复留為應奉。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Hanlin Attendant for Documents, still concurrently compiler; transferred to University Assistant Instructor, then again retained as Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Hanlin Attendant for Documents, still concurrently compiler; transferred to University Assistant Instructor, then again retained as Attendant.

sentences.zh: 南歸省母，旋復召還。

translations.literal: He returned south to visit his mother, and was soon summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: He returned south to visit his mother and was soon summoned back.

sentences.zh: 傒斯凡三入翰林，朝廷之事，臺閣之儀，靡不閒習，集賢學士王約謂：「與傒斯談治道，大起人意，授之以政，當無施不可。」

translations.literal: Xisi thrice entered the Hanlin; court affairs and censorate ritual—none was he not well practiced in. Academician Wang Yue of the Academy of Assembled Worthies said: 'Talking governance with Xisi greatly stirs one's mind; grant him administration and there should be nothing he cannot apply.'
translations.idiomatic: Xisi entered the Hanlin three times and was well practiced in court affairs and censorate ritual. Academician Wang Yue said, 'Talking governance with Xisi greatly stirs the mind; grant him office and there should be nothing he cannot do.'

sentences.zh: 天歷初，開奎章閣，首擢為授經郎，以教勳戚大臣子孫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianli the Kuizhang Pavilion was opened; he was first elevated to Lecturer of the Classics to teach the sons and grandsons of meritorious kin and great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianli the Kuizhang Pavilion was opened; he was first elevated to Lecturer of the Classics to teach the sons of meritorious kin and great ministers.

sentences.zh: 文宗時幸閣中，有所諮訪，奏對稱旨，恆以字呼之而不名。

translations.literal: Wenzong from time to time visited the pavilion and had consultations; his memorial replies accorded with intent, and the emperor constantly called him by style without using his name.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong often visited the pavilion for consultation; his replies accorded with the emperor's intent, and the emperor constantly called him by style without using his name.

sentences.zh: 每中書奏用儒臣，必問曰：「其材何如揭曼碩？」

translations.literal: Whenever the Secretariat memorialized to employ Confucian ministers he invariably asked: 'How does his talent compare with Jie Manshuo?'
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Secretariat memorialized to employ Confucian ministers he invariably asked, 'How does his talent compare with Jie Manshuo?'

sentences.zh: 間出所上《太平政要策》以示台臣，曰：「此朕授經郎揭曼碩所進也。」

translations.literal: From time to time he produced the Essential Policies for Great Peace that Xisi had submitted and showed censorial ministers, saying: 'This was submitted by my Lecturer of the Classics Jie Manshuo.'
translations.idiomatic: From time to time he produced the Essential Policies for Great Peace that Xisi had submitted and showed censorial ministers, saying, 'This was submitted by my Lecturer of the Classics Jie Manshuo.'

sentences.zh: 其見親重如此。

translations.literal: Such was the intimacy and weight he received.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the favor he received.

sentences.zh: 富州地不產金，官府惑於奸民之言，為募淘金戶三百，而以其人總之，散往他郡，採金以獻，歲課自四兩累增至四十九兩。

translations.literal: Fuzhou's land did not produce gold, but officials were deluded by treacherous people's words and recruited three hundred gold-panning households, placing one man in overall charge; they were dispersed to other prefectures to gather gold for presentation, the annual levy rising from four taels cumulatively to forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Fuzhou's land did not produce gold, but officials were deluded by treacherous people's words and recruited three hundred gold-panning households under one overseer, dispersed to other prefectures to gather gold for tribute, the annual levy rising from four taels to forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 其人既死，而三百戶所存無甚一，又貧不聊生，有司遂責民之受役於官者代輸，民多以是破產。

translations.literal: When that man died scarcely one of the three hundred households remained, and they were again too poor to live; officials then charged the people who had received corvée from the government to pay in their stead, and many families were ruined thereby.
translations.idiomatic: When that overseer died scarcely one of the three hundred households remained, and they were too poor to live; officials then charged corvée laborers to pay in their stead, and many families were ruined.

sentences.zh: 中書因傒斯言，遂蠲其徵，民賴以蘇，富州人至今德之。

translations.literal: The Secretariat, because of Xisi's words, then remitted the levy; the people relied on this for revival, and the people of Fuzhou to this day honor his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat, because of Xisi's words, remitted the levy; the people revived, and the people of Fuzhou honor him to this day.

sentences.zh: 與修《經世大典》，文宗取其所撰《憲典》讀之，顧謂近臣曰：「此豈非《唐律》乎！」

translations.literal: He participated in compiling the Great Compendium for Governing the Age; Wenzong took his Constitutional Canon to read and, turning to nearby ministers, said: 'Is this not the Tang Code!'
translations.idiomatic: He participated in compiling the Great Compendium for Governing the Age; Wenzong read his Constitutional Canon and, turning to nearby ministers, said, 'Is this not the Tang Code!'

sentences.zh: 特授藝文監丞，參檢校書籍事，且屢稱其純實，欲進用之，會文宗崩而止。

translations.literal: He was specially appointed Deputy Director of the Bureau of Arts and Letters, participating in inspection and collation of books; moreover he was repeatedly praised as pure and solid, and the emperor wished to advance him— but it stopped when Wenzong died.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially appointed Deputy Director of the Bureau of Arts and Letters, participating in inspection of books; he was repeatedly praised as pure and solid, and the emperor wished to advance him—but Wenzong died before this could happen.

sentences.zh: 元統初，詔對便殿，慰諭良久，命賜以諸王所服表裡各一，躬自辯識以授之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuantong he was ordered to audience in the informal hall; consolation and instruction lasted long, and he was commanded to be granted one outer and inner garment each as princes wore, the emperor personally distinguishing and bestowing them.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuantong he was summoned to the informal hall; the emperor consoled him at length and granted one outer and inner garment each as princes wore, personally selecting and bestowing them.

sentences.zh: 適翰林待制，升集賢學士，階中順大夫。

translations.literal: He was made Attendant Draftsman of the Hanlin Academy, promoted to Academician of the Academy of Assembled Worthies, rank Grand Master for Court Order.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Attendant Draftsman of the Hanlin Academy, promoted to Academician of the Academy of Assembled Worthies, rank Grand Master for Court Order.

sentences.zh: 先是，儒學官赴吏部銓者，必移集賢，考較其所業，集賢下國子監，監下博士，吏文淹稽，動逾累月。

translations.literal: Earlier, Confucian officials who went to the Ministry of Personnel for selection had to be transferred to the Academy of Assembled Worthies to compare their accomplishments; the Academy sent them down to the Imperial University, the University down to erudites—clerical documents delayed and stagnated, often exceeding many months.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Confucian officials who went to the Ministry of Personnel for selection had to be transferred to the Academy of Assembled Worthies for evaluation; the Academy sent them to the Imperial University, the University to erudites—clerical delays often exceeded many months.

sentences.zh: 傒斯請更其法，以事付本院屬官，人甚便之。

translations.literal: Xisi requested to change this method, entrusting matters to subordinate officials of his bureau; people found it very convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Xisi requested to change this method, entrusting matters to subordinate officials of his bureau; people found it very convenient.

sentences.zh: 奉旨祠北岳、濟瀆、南鎮，便道西還，時秦王伯顏當國，屢促其還，傒斯引疾固辭。

translations.literal: By imperial order he sacrificed at Mount Heng, the Ji and Du rivers, and the Southern Marchmount, returning west by convenient route. At the time Prince of Qin Bayan held the state and repeatedly urged his return; Xisi pleaded illness and firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order he sacrificed at Mount Heng, the Ji and Du rivers, and the Southern Marchmount, returning west by convenient route. At the time Prince of Qin Bayan held power and repeatedly urged his return; Xisi pleaded illness and firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 既而天子親擢為奎章閣供奉學士，乃即日就道，未至，改翰林直學士，及開經筵，再升侍講學士、同知經筵事，以對品進階中奉大夫。

translations.literal: Before long the Son of Heaven personally elevated him to Offering Academician of the Kuizhang Pavilion; he set out the same day. Before arriving he was changed to Direct Academician of the Hanlin Academy; when the classic lectures opened he was again promoted to Academician-Expounder and Associate Director of Classic Lectures, advancing by matched rank to Grand Master for Court Service.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the emperor personally elevated him to Offering Academician of the Kuizhang Pavilion; he set out the same day. Before arriving he was made Direct Academician of the Hanlin Academy; when classic lectures opened he was promoted to Academician-Expounder and Associate Director of Classic Lectures, advancing to Grand Master for Court Service.

sentences.zh: 時新格超升不越二等，獨傒斯進四等，轉九階，蓋異數也。

translations.literal: At the time the new regulations for extraordinary promotion did not exceed two grades; Xisi alone advanced four grades, transferring nine steps—an exceptional number.
translations.idiomatic: At the time new regulations limited extraordinary promotion to two grades; Xisi alone advanced four grades, nine steps—an exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 經筵無專官，曰領曰知，多宰執大臣，故微辭奧義，必屬傒斯訂定而後進，其言往往寓獻替之誠，務以裨益治道。

translations.literal: The classic lectures had no dedicated office—titles were 'director' and 'associate'—mostly held by chief councilors and great ministers; therefore subtle words and profound meanings had to be entrusted to Xisi for revision before submission. His words often lodged the sincerity of offering replacement, striving to benefit the way of governance.
translations.idiomatic: Classic lectures had no dedicated office—titles were 'director' and 'associate'—mostly held by chief councilors; therefore subtle words and profound meanings had to be revised by Xisi before submission. His words often lodged sincere counsel, striving to benefit governance.

sentences.zh: 天子嘉其忠懇，數出金織文段以賜。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven praised his loyal earnestness and repeatedly issued gold-woven brocade segments as gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his loyal earnestness and repeatedly granted gold-woven brocade.

sentences.zh: 至正三年，年七十，致其事而去，詔遣使追及於漷南。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhizheng, at seventy, he resigned his duties and left; an edict sent envoys to overtake him at Huo south of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhizheng, at seventy, he resigned and left; an edict sent envoys to overtake him south of the capital.

sentences.zh: 尋复奉上尊諭旨，還撰《明宗神御殿碑》，文成，賜楮幣萬緡、白金五十兩，中宮賜白金亦如之。

translations.literal: Soon he again received imperial instruction to return and compose the Stele for Emperor Mingzong's Spirit Hall; when the text was finished he was granted ten thousand strings of paper money and fifty taels of white metal; the empress also granted white metal likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he received imperial instruction to return and compose the Stele for Emperor Mingzong's Spirit Hall; when finished he was granted ten thousand strings of paper money and fifty taels of silver; the empress granted silver likewise.

sentences.zh: 求去，不許，命丞相脫脫及執政大臣面諭毋行，傒斯曰：「使揭傒斯有一得之獻，諸公用其言而天下蒙其利，雖死於此，何恨！

translations.literal: He sought to leave but was not permitted; the chief councilor Toghto and administering great ministers were ordered to instruct him face to face not to go. Xisi said: 'If Jie Xisi had one attainment to offer, and you all used his words so the realm received the benefit—even if I died here, what regret!
translations.idiomatic: He sought to leave but was not permitted; Chief Councilor Toghto and senior ministers were ordered to tell him face to face not to go. Xisi said, 'If I had one useful counsel and you all used it so the realm benefited—even if I died here, what regret!

sentences.zh: 不然，何益之有！」

translations.literal: Otherwise, what benefit would there be!'
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, what benefit would there be!'

sentences.zh: 丞相因問：「方今政治何先？」

translations.literal: The chief councilor then asked: 'In present governance, what comes first?'
translations.idiomatic: The chief councilor then asked, 'In present governance, what comes first?'

sentences.zh: 傒斯曰：「儲材為先，養之於位望未隆之時，而用之於周密庶務之後，則無失材廢事之患矣。」

translations.literal: Xisi said: 'Storing talent comes first—nurturing them when rank and reputation are not yet lofty, and employing them after comprehensive minor affairs—then there will be no worry of losing talent and abandoning business.'
translations.idiomatic: Xisi said, 'Storing talent comes first—nurturing them before rank and reputation are lofty, and employing them after they have mastered comprehensive affairs—then there will be no worry of losing talent or abandoning business.'

sentences.zh: 一日，集議朝堂，傒斯抗言：「當兼行新舊銅錢，以救鈔法之弊。」

translations.literal: One day, gathered in deliberation at court, Xisi spoke forthrightly: 'We ought concurrently to employ new and old copper cash to rescue the abuses of paper money.'
translations.idiomatic: One day at court deliberation Xisi spoke forthrightly, 'We ought to employ new and old copper cash concurrently to rescue the abuses of paper money.'

sentences.zh: 執政言不可，傒斯持之​​益力，丞相雖稱其不阿，而竟莫行其言也。

translations.literal: The administrators said it could not be done; Xisi held to it ever more forcefully. Though the chief councilor praised him for not flattering, in the end his words were not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The administrators said it could not be done; Xisi argued ever more forcefully. Though the chief councilor praised him for not flattering, in the end his proposal was not adopted.

sentences.zh: 詔修遼、金、宋三史，傒斯與為總裁官，丞相問：「修史以何為本？」

translations.literal: An edict ordered compilation of the histories of Liao, Jin, and Song; Xisi served as chief editor. The chief councilor asked: 'In compiling history, what is fundamental?'
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered compilation of the histories of Liao, Jin, and Song; Xisi served as chief editor. The chief councilor asked, 'In compiling history, what is fundamental?'

sentences.zh: 曰：「用人為本，有學問文章而不知史事者，不可與；

translations.literal: He said: 'Employing people is fundamental. Those with learning and literary composition who do not know historical affairs may not be given the task;
translations.idiomatic: He said, 'Employing people is fundamental. Those with learning and literary skill who do not know historical affairs may not be given the task;

sentences.zh: 有學問文章知史事而心術不正者，不可與。

translations.literal: those with learning, literary composition, and knowledge of historical affairs but whose mind-methods are not correct may not be given it.
translations.idiomatic: those with learning, literary skill, and knowledge of historical affairs but whose character is not upright may not be given it.

sentences.zh: 用人之道，又當以心術為本也。」

translations.literal: In the way of employing people, one must again take mind-method as fundamental.'
translations.idiomatic: In employing people, character must again be fundamental.'

sentences.zh: 且與僚屬言：「欲求作史之法，須求作史之意。

translations.literal: Moreover he told subordinates: 'If you wish to seek the method of writing history, you must seek the intent of writing history.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover he told subordinates, 'To seek the method of writing history, you must seek the intent of writing history.

sentences.zh: 古人作史，雖小善必錄，小惡必記。

translations.literal: The ancients writing history, though the good was small they must record it; though the evil was small they must note it.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients writing history recorded even small good deeds and noted even small evils.

sentences.zh: 不然，何以示懲勸！」

translations.literal: Otherwise, how could one display punishment and encouragement!'
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, how could one display punishment and encouragement!'

sentences.zh: 由是顏然以筆削自任，凡政事得失，人材賢否，一律以是非之公。

translations.literal: Thereby he visibly took the brush and cutting upon himself; in all gains and losses of government affairs, worthiness or unworthiness of personnel, he uniformly applied the public standard of right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Thereby he visibly took editorial responsibility upon himself; in all gains and losses of government and worthiness of personnel, he uniformly applied the public standard of right and wrong.

sentences.zh: 至於物論之不齊，必反覆辨論，以求歸於至當而後止。

translations.literal: As for uneven popular opinion, he invariably debated back and forth, seeking to return to utmost propriety before stopping.
translations.idiomatic: When popular opinion was divided, he invariably debated back and forth until utmost propriety was reached.

sentences.zh: 四年，《遼史》成，有旨獎諭，仍督早成金、宋二史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the History of Liao was completed; an order commended and instructed, still urging early completion of the Jin and Song histories.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the History of Liao was completed; an order commended the work and still urged early completion of the Jin and Song histories.

sentences.zh: 傒斯留宿史館，朝夕不敢休，因得寒疾，七日卒。

translations.literal: Xisi lodged overnight in the History Office, morning and evening not daring to rest; he thereby contracted a cold illness and died in seven days.
translations.idiomatic: Xisi lodged overnight in the History Office, morning and evening not daring to rest; he contracted a cold illness and died in seven days.

sentences.zh: 時方有使者至自上京，錫宴史局，以傒斯故，改宴日。

translations.literal: At the time an envoy had just arrived from the Upper Capital to grant a feast to the History Bureau; because of Xisi the feast day was changed.
translations.idiomatic: At the time an envoy had just arrived from the Upper Capital to grant a feast to the History Bureau; because of Xisi the feast day was changed.

sentences.zh: 使者以聞，帝為嗟悼，賜楮幣萬緡，仍給驛舟，護送其喪歸江南。

translations.literal: The envoy reported upward; the emperor sighed in mourning, granted ten thousand strings of paper money, and still provided relay boats to escort his coffin home to Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy reported upward; the emperor mourned, granted ten thousand strings of paper money, and provided relay boats to escort his coffin home to Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 六年，制贈護軍，追封豫章郡公，諡曰文安。

translations.literal: In the sixth year an order posthumously granted Defender of the Army, with posthumous enfeoffment as Duke of Yuzhang Commandery and temple name Wen'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year an order posthumously granted Defender of the Army, enfeoffed posthumously as Duke of Yuzhang Commandery, with the temple name Wen'an.

sentences.zh: 有勳爵而無官階者，有司失之也。

translations.literal: To have meritorious rank without official grade was an error of the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: To have meritorious rank without official grade was an error of the responsible offices.

sentences.zh: 傒斯少處窮約，事親菽水粗具而必得其歡心，既有祿入，衣食稍逾於前，輒愀然曰：「吾親未嘗享是也。」

translations.literal: Xisi in youth dwelt in poverty and constraint; serving his parents, bean broth and water were roughly sufficient yet he invariably won their joyful hearts. Once he had salary income, when food and clothing slightly exceeded before he would look sorrowful and say: 'My parents never enjoyed this.'
translations.idiomatic: Xisi in youth lived in poverty; serving his parents, plain food and water sufficed yet he invariably won their affection. Once he had salary, when food and clothing slightly exceeded what they had known he would look sorrowful and say, 'My parents never enjoyed this.'

sentences.zh: 故平生清儉，至老不渝。

translations.literal: Therefore in life he was pure and frugal, to old age without change.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore he lived pure and frugal to the end of his days.

sentences.zh: 友於兄弟，終始無間言。

translations.literal: He was friendly with his brothers; from beginning to end there was no estranged speech.
translations.idiomatic: He was friendly with his brothers; from beginning to end there was no estrangement.

sentences.zh: 立朝雖居散地，而急於薦士，揚人之善惟恐不及，而聞吏之貪墨病民者，則尤不曲為之掩覆也。

translations.literal: Though at court he occupied a loose post, he was eager to recommend scholars, promoting others' goodness fearing he could not reach enough; yet when he heard of clerks' corruption harming the people, he especially would not bend to cover it for them.
translations.idiomatic: Though at court he held a loose post, he was eager to recommend scholars and promote others' virtues as much as he could; yet when he heard of corrupt clerks harming the people, he especially would not cover for them.

sentences.zh: 為文章，敘事嚴整，語簡而當；

translations.literal: In composing essays his narrative was strict and orderly, his language concise and apt;
translations.idiomatic: In prose his narrative was strict and orderly, his language concise and apt;

sentences.zh: 詩尤清婉麗密；

translations.literal: his poetry especially clear, gentle, beautiful, and dense;
translations.idiomatic: his poetry especially clear, gentle, and refined;

sentences.zh: 善楷書、行、草。

translations.literal: he was skilled in regular script, running script, and cursive.
translations.idiomatic: he was skilled in regular, running, and cursive script.

sentences.zh: 朝廷大典冊及元勳茂德當得銘辭者，必以命焉。

translations.literal: For great court compendia and meritorious elders of flourishing virtue who ought to receive inscription texts, he was invariably entrusted with the task.
translations.idiomatic: For great court compendia and meritorious elders deserving inscription texts, he was invariably entrusted with the task.

sentences.zh: 殊方絕域，咸慕其名，得其文者，莫不以為榮云。

translations.literal: Remote regions and distant lands all admired his name; those who obtained his writings none failed to regard it as glory.
translations.idiomatic: Remote regions all admired his name; those who obtained his writings regarded it as an honor.

sentences.zh: ○黃鳷

translations.literal: ○ Huang Jin
translations.idiomatic: ○ Huang Jin

sentences.zh: 黃溍，字晉卿，婺州義烏人。

translations.literal: Huang Jin, styled Jinqing, was a man of Yiwu in Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Jin, whose style was Jinqing, came from Yiwu in Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 母童氏，夢大星墜於懷，乃有娠，歷二十四月始生溍。

translations.literal: His mother, the Tong clan, dreamed a great star fell into her bosom and then conceived; after twenty-four months Jin was born.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, of the Tong clan, dreamed a great star fell into her bosom and conceived; after twenty-four months Jin was born.

sentences.zh: 溍生而俊異，比成童，授以書詩，不一月成誦。

translations.literal: Jin was born handsome and unusual; when he reached boyhood they taught him books and poetry, and in less than a month he could recite.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was born handsome and unusual; when he reached boyhood they taught him books and poetry, and in less than a month he could recite them.

sentences.zh: 迨長，以文名於四方。

translations.literal: When he grew he was famed for literature in all directions.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew he was famed for literature throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 中延祐二年進士第，授台州寧海丞。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Yanyou and was appointed assistant magistrate of Ninghai in Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Yanyou and was appointed assistant magistrate of Ninghai in Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 縣地瀕鹽場，亭戶恃其不統於有司，肆毒害民；

translations.literal: The county bordered salt works; saltern households relied on not being under officials and wantonly harmed the people;
translations.idiomatic: The county bordered salt works; saltern households, not under regular officials, wantonly harmed the people;

sentences.zh: 編戶隸漕司及財賦府者，亦謂各有所憑，橫暴尤甚。

translations.literal: registered households subordinate to the transport commission and revenue bureau also claimed each had backing, and their violence was especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: registered households under the transport commission and revenue bureau also claimed backing, and their violence was especially severe.

sentences.zh: 溍皆痛繩以法，吏以利害白，弗顧也。

translations.literal: Jin all sternly punished them by law; clerks reported gain and loss, but he paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: Jin sternly punished them all by law; clerks warned of consequences, but he paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 民有後母與僧通而ＣＧ殺其父者，反誣民所為，獄將成，溍變衣冠陰察之，具知其奸偽，卒直其冤。

translations.literal: There was a man whose stepmother, having relations with a monk, together killed his father, then falsely accused the son of doing it. The case was about to be concluded when Jin changed his dress and secretly investigated, fully knowing the fraud, and in the end righted his wrong.
translations.idiomatic: A man's stepmother, having relations with a monk, together killed his father, then falsely accused the son. The case was about to close when Jin investigated in disguise, fully uncovered the fraud, and righted the son's wrong.

sentences.zh: 惡少年名在盜籍者，而謀為劫奪，未行，邑大姓執之，圖中賞格。

translations.literal: Wicked youths whose names were on the bandit register plotted robbery but had not acted; a great clan of the district seized them, aiming at the reward scale.
translations.idiomatic: Wicked youths on the bandit register plotted robbery but had not acted; a great clan of the district seized them, aiming at the reward.

sentences.zh: 初無獲財左驗，事久不決，溍為之疏剔，以其獄上，論之如本條，免死者十餘人。

translations.literal: At first there was no proof of seized property; the matter long went unresolved. Jin clarified and sifted it for them, submitted the case upward, and judged according to the original statute, sparing more than ten from death.
translations.idiomatic: At first there was no proof of seized property; the matter long went unresolved. Jin clarified the case, submitted it upward, and judged according to the statute, sparing more than ten from death.

sentences.zh: 遷兩浙都轉運鹽使司石堰西場監運，改諸既州判官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to transport supervisor of the Shiyan West Field of the Liang-Zhe Salt Transport Commission, then changed to vice-prefect of Zhuji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to transport supervisor of the Shiyan West Field of the Liang-Zhe Salt Transport Commission, then made vice-prefect of Zhuji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 巡海官舸，例以三載一新，費出於官，而責足於民。

translations.literal: Coast-guard official vessels by precedent were renewed every three years; costs came from the government but full payment was charged to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Coast-guard vessels by precedent were renewed every three years; costs came from the government but full payment was charged to the people.

sentences.zh: 有餘，則總其事者私焉。

translations.literal: If there was surplus, the one overseeing the matter kept it privately.
translations.idiomatic: Surplus funds were kept privately by those in charge.

sentences.zh: 溍撙節浮蠹，以餘錢還民，歡呼而去。

translations.literal: Jin restrained floating corruption, returning surplus money to the people, who cheered as they departed.
translations.idiomatic: Jin cut wasteful corruption and returned surplus money to the people, who cheered as they departed.

sentences.zh: 奸民以偽鈔鉤結黨與，脅攘人財，官若吏聽其謀，挾往新昌、天台、寧海、東陽諸縣，株連所及數百家，民受禍至慘。

translations.literal: Treacherous people used counterfeit notes to hook accomplices and extort others' wealth; officials and clerks followed their schemes, carrying cases to Xinchang, Tiantai, Ninghai, Dongyang, and other counties; implicated families reached hundreds, and the people's suffering was extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Criminals used counterfeit notes to form gangs and extort wealth; officials followed their schemes, carrying cases to Xinchang, Tiantai, Ninghai, Dongyang, and other counties; hundreds of families were implicated and the people's suffering was extreme.

sentences.zh: 郡府下溍鞫治，溍一問，皆引伏，官吏除名，同謀者各杖遣之。

translations.literal: The prefectural government sent Jin to try the case; with one question all confessed; officials were struck from the register and accomplices each beaten and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectural government sent Jin to try the case; with one question all confessed; officials were dismissed and accomplices beaten and sent away.

sentences.zh: 有盜係於錢唐縣獄，遊民賂獄吏私縱之，假署文牒，發其來為嚮導，逮捕二十餘家。

translations.literal: A bandit was held in Qiantang County jail; a vagrant bribed jail clerks to release him privately, forged an official document, and brought him as guide, seizing more than twenty households.
translations.idiomatic: A bandit was held in Qiantang County jail; a vagrant bribed jail clerks to release him, forged documents, used him as a guide, and seized more than twenty households.

sentences.zh: 溍訪得其情，以正盜宜傅重議，持偽文書來者又非州民，俱械還錢唐，誣者自明。

translations.literal: Jin investigated and obtained the truth: the true bandit ought to bear heavy sentence, while those bearing forged documents were not prefecture natives—all were shackled and returned to Qiantang, and the falsely accused cleared themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Jin investigated and learned the truth: the true bandit deserved heavy sentence, while those with forged documents were not natives of the prefecture—all were returned to Qiantang in custody, and the falsely accused were cleared.

sentences.zh: 入為應奉翰林文字、同知制誥，兼國史院編修官，轉國子博士。

translations.literal: He entered court as Hanlin Attendant for Documents and Associate Director of Edicts, concurrently Compiler of the National History Office, then transferred to University Erudite.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Hanlin Attendant for Documents and Associate Director of Edicts, concurrently Compiler of the National History Office, then became University Erudite.

sentences.zh: 視弟子如朋交，未始以師道自尊，輕納人拜，而來學者滋益恭，業成而仕，皆有聞於世。

translations.literal: He regarded disciples as friends and companions, never taking the teacher's way to elevate himself or lightly accepting others' bows; yet those who came to study grew ever more respectful, and when their work was done and they entered office, all had reputation in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He regarded disciples as friends, never elevating himself as a teacher or lightly accepting bows; yet students grew ever more respectful, and when they entered office all gained reputation in the world.

sentences.zh: 時欲增設禮殿配位四，配位合東坐而西向，學官或議分置於左右，同列不敢爭，氵晉獨面折之，事乃止。

translations.literal: At the time they wished to add four associated seats in the ritual hall; associated seats should sit east facing west. Some school officials debated placing them left and right; colleagues did not dare dispute, but Jin alone confronted them face to face and the matter stopped.
translations.idiomatic: At the time they wished to add four associated seats in the ritual hall, which should sit east facing west. Some school officials debated placing them left and right; colleagues did not dare dispute, but Jin alone confronted them and the matter stopped.

sentences.zh: 出為江浙等處儒學提舉。

translations.literal: He went out as Confucian Education Intendant for Jiang-Zhe and other regions.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Confucian Education Intendant for Jiang-Zhe and other regions.

sentences.zh: 溍年始六十七，不俟引年，亟上納祿侍親之請，絕江徑歸。

translations.literal: Jin was only sixty-seven, not waiting for the retirement age; he urgently submitted a request to surrender salary and attend his parents, crossed the river straight home.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was only sixty-seven and did not wait for retirement age; he urgently requested to surrender his salary and care for his parents, crossed the river, and went straight home.

sentences.zh: 俄以秘書少監致仕，未幾，落致仕，除翰林直學士、知制誥同修國史。

translations.literal: Soon he retired as Vice Director of the Secretariat; before long retirement was revoked and he was appointed Direct Academician of the Hanlin Academy, Director of Edicts, and concurrent Compiler of the National History.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he retired as Vice Director of the Secretariat; before long retirement was revoked and he was appointed Direct Academician of the Hanlin Academy, Director of Edicts, and concurrent Compiler of the National History.

sentences.zh: 尋兼經筵官，執經進講者三十有二，帝嘉其忠，數出金織紋段賜之。

translations.literal: Soon he also served in the classic lectures, holding the classics and lecturing thirty-two times; the emperor praised his loyalty and repeatedly issued gold-woven brocade segments as gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he also served in the classic lectures, lecturing thirty-two times; the emperor praised his loyalty and repeatedly granted gold-woven brocade.

sentences.zh: 升侍講學士、知制誥同修國史、同知經筵事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Academician-Expounder, Director of Edicts, concurrent Compiler of the National History, and Associate Director of Classic Lectures.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Academician-Expounder, Director of Edicts, concurrent Compiler of the National History, and Associate Director of Classic Lectures.

sentences.zh: 階自將仕郎七轉至中奉大夫。

translations.literal: His rank rose through seven steps from Gentleman for Merit to Grand Master for Court Service.
translations.idiomatic: His rank rose through seven steps from Gentleman for Merit to Grand Master for Court Service.

sentences.zh: 几上章求歸，不俟報而行，帝聞之，遣使者追還京師，復為前官。

translations.literal: Several times he memorialized seeking to return, departing without awaiting reply; when the emperor heard he sent envoys to overtake him and bring him back to the capital, restoring his former offices.
translations.idiomatic: Several times he memorialized seeking to return and departed without awaiting reply; when the emperor heard he sent envoys to bring him back to the capital and restored his former offices.

sentences.zh: 久之，始得謝南還，優游田里間，凡七年，卒於繡湖之私第，年八十一。

translations.literal: After long delay he at last obtained leave to return south, leisurely in fields and villages for seven years in all; he died at his private residence by Embroidered Lake at the age of eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: After long delay he obtained leave to return south and lived leisurely in the countryside for seven years; he died at his private residence by Embroidered Lake at the age of eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 贈中奉大夫、江西等處行中書省參知政事、護軍，追封江夏郡公，諡曰文獻。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Grand Master for Court Service, Vice Governor of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat and other regions, and Defender of the Army; posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Jiangxia Commandery with temple name Wenxian.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously granted Grand Master for Court Service, Vice Governor of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat, and Defender of the Army; enfeoffed posthumously as Duke of Jiangxia Commandery with the temple name Wenxian.

sentences.zh: 溍天資介特，在州縣唯以清白為治，月俸弗給，每鬻產以佐其費。

translations.literal: Jin's native endowment was upright and special; in prefectures and counties he governed solely by purity and clarity, his monthly salary insufficient, each time selling property to supplement his expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was upright by nature; in prefectures and counties he governed solely with integrity, his salary insufficient, and he often sold property to cover his expenses.

sentences.zh: 及升朝行，挺立無所附，足不登巨公勢人之門，君子稱其清風高節，如冰壺玉尺，纖塵弗污。

translations.literal: When he rose to court service he stood erect without attaching to anyone, his feet never entering the gates of great lords and men of power; gentlemen praised his pure wind and lofty integrity, like an ice jug or jade measure—fine dust could not stain it.
translations.idiomatic: When he rose to court he stood erect without attaching to anyone and never entered the gates of great lords; gentlemen praised his pure integrity, like an ice jug or jade measure unstained by dust.

sentences.zh: 然剛中少容，觸物或弦急霆震，若未易涯涘，一旋踵間，煦如陽春。

translations.literal: Yet his firm center had little tolerance; encountering things he sometimes was like a drawn bowstring or sudden thunder, as if hard to bound—yet in the turn of a heel he was warm as spring sun.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was firm and impatient; encountering provocation he could be sudden as thunder, yet in the next moment warm as spring sun.

sentences.zh: 溍之學，博極天下之書，而約之於至精，剖析經史疑難，及古今因革制度名物之屬，旁引曲證，多先儒所未發。

translations.literal: Jin's learning exhaustively reached books throughout the realm yet condensed them to utmost refinement; analyzing difficulties in classics and histories, and matters of institutions and names past and present, with indirect citation and curved proof—much that earlier Confucians had not brought forth.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's learning ranged across books throughout the realm yet condensed them to utmost refinement; analyzing difficulties in classics and histories and matters of institutions and names past and present, with wide citation—much that earlier Confucians had not brought forth.

sentences.zh: 文辭佈置謹嚴，援據精切，俯仰雍容，不大聲色，譬之澄湖不波，一碧萬頃，魚鱉蛟龍，潛伏不動，而淵然之光，自不可犯。

translations.literal: His literary phrasing was arranged with strict care, citations precise and apt, bearing composed and easy without great sound or color—like a clear lake without waves, ten thousand acres of one blue-green, fish, turtles, and dragons lurking unmoving, yet the deep light itself could not be violated.
translations.idiomatic: His prose was arranged with strict care, citations precise, bearing composed and easy without loud display—like a clear lake without waves, ten thousand acres of blue-green, fish and dragons lurking unmoving, yet its deep light could not be violated.

sentences.zh: 所著書，有《日損齋稿》三十三卷、《義烏志》七卷、《筆記》一卷。

translations.literal: Books he authored include Drafts from the Daily Loss Studio in thirty-three fascicles, Gazetteer of Yiwu in seven fascicles, and Notes in one fascicle.
translations.idiomatic: His works include Drafts from the Daily Loss Studio in thirty-three fascicles, Gazetteer of Yiwu in seven fascicles, and Notes in one fascicle.

sentences.zh: 同郡柳貫、吳萊，皆浦陽人。

translations.literal: Liu Guan and Wu Lai of the same commandery were both men of Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Guan and Wu Lai of the same commandery were both from Puyang.

sentences.zh: 貫​​字道傳，器局凝定，端嚴若神。

translations.literal: Guan, styled Daochuan, had a bearing settled and firm, dignified as if divine.
translations.idiomatic: Guan, styled Daochuan, had a settled bearing, dignified as if divine.

sentences.zh: 嘗受性理之學於蘭溪金履祥，必見諸躬行，自幼至老，好學不倦。

translations.literal: He once received the learning of nature and principle from Jin Lüxiang of Lanxi, invariably manifesting it in personal conduct; from youth to old age he loved learning without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: He studied Neo-Confucian learning with Jin Lüxiang of Lanxi and invariably put it into practice; from youth to old age he loved learning without weariness.

sentences.zh: 凡《六經》、百氏、兵刑、律曆、數術、方技、異教外書，靡所不通。

translations.literal: All the Six Classics, the hundred schools, military law and punishment, calendars and astronomy, numerology, arts and techniques, and foreign books of heterodox teachings—none was he not versed in.
translations.idiomatic: The Six Classics, the hundred schools, military law, calendars, numerology, arts, and foreign heterodox texts—none was beyond his knowledge.

sentences.zh: 作文沉鬱舂容，涵肆演迤，人多傳誦之。

translations.literal: His essays were deep, somber, and harmonious, expansive and flowing; many transmitted and recited them.
translations.idiomatic: His essays were deep, somber, and harmonious, expansive and flowing; many transmitted and recited them.

sentences.zh: 始用察舉為江山縣儒學教諭，仕至翰林待制。

translations.literal: He first entered through investigation and recommendation as Confucian instructor of Jiangshan County, rising in office to Hanlin Attendant Draftsman.
translations.idiomatic: He first entered through recommendation as Confucian instructor of Jiangshan County and rose to Hanlin Attendant Draftsman.

sentences.zh: 與溍及臨川虞集、豫章揭傒斯齊名，人號為儒林四傑。

translations.literal: He was famed equally with Jin, Yu Ji of Linchuan, and Jie Xisi of Yuzhang; people called them the Four Heroes of the Confucian Grove.
translations.idiomatic: He was famed equally with Jin, Yu Ji of Linchuan, and Jie Xisi of Yuzhang; people called them the Four Heroes of the Confucian Grove.

sentences.zh: 所著書，有文集四十卷、《字系》二卷、《近思錄廣輯》三卷、《金石竹帛遺文》十卷。

translations.literal: Books he authored include a collection of writings in forty fascicles, Genealogy of Characters in two fascicles, Expanded Compilation of Reflections on Things Near in three fascicles, and Surviving Texts on Metal, Stone, Bamboo, and Silk in ten fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: His works include collected writings in forty fascicles, Genealogy of Characters in two fascicles, Expanded Compilation of Reflections on Things Near in three fascicles, and Surviving Texts on Metal, Stone, Bamboo, and Silk in ten fascicles.

sentences.zh: 年七十三卒。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 萊字立夫，集賢大學士直方之子也，輩行稍後於貫、溍。

translations.literal: Lai, styled Lifu, was son of Academician-in-Chief Zhifang of the Academy of Assembled Worthies; his generation was slightly after Guan and Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Lai, styled Lifu, was son of Academician-in-Chief Zhifang of the Academy of Assembled Worthies; his generation was slightly junior to Guan and Jin.

sentences.zh: 天資絕人，七歲能屬文，凡書一經目，輒成誦，嘗往族父家，日易《漢書》一帙以去，族父迫扣之，萊瑯然而誦，不遺一字，三易他編，皆如之，眾驚以為神。

translations.literal: His native talent surpassed others; at seven he could compose essays. Whatever book passed once before his eyes he at once could recite. Once visiting a clansman's home he daily exchanged one fascicle of the Book of Han to take away; the clansman urgently tested him and Lai recited it ringing clear without missing a character. Three times he changed to other sections—all the same—and the crowd marveled, considering him divine.
translations.idiomatic: His talent surpassed others; at seven he could compose essays. Whatever book he glanced at he memorized. Once visiting a clansman's home he borrowed one fascicle of the Book of Han daily; the clansman tested him and Lai recited it without missing a character. Three times he changed sections—all the same—and onlookers marveled as if he were divine.

sentences.zh: 延祐七年，以《春秋》舉上禮部，不利，退居深裊山中，益窮諸書奧旨，著《尚書標說》六卷、《春秋世變圖》二卷、《春秋傳授譜》一卷、《古職方錄》八卷、《孟子弟子列傳》二卷、《楚漢正聲》二卷、《樂府類編》一百卷、《唐律刪要》三十卷、文集六十卷。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yanyou he was presented to the Ministry of Rites on the Spring and Autumn Annals but was unsuccessful; he retired to deep mountains in Shen'ao, further exhausting the subtle purport of all books, and authored Expository Marks on the Documents in six fascicles, Charts of Changes through the Ages in the Spring and Autumn in two fascicles, Genealogy of Transmission of the Spring and Autumn in one fascicle, Record of Ancient Regional Offices in eight fascicles, Biographies of Mencius's Disciples in two fascicles, Correct Sounds of Chu and Han in two fascicles, Classified Compilation of Music Bureau Poems in one hundred fascicles, Abridged Essentials of Tang Lyric Rules in thirty fascicles, and collected works in sixty fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Yanyou he was presented to the Ministry of Rites on the Spring and Autumn Annals but failed; he retired to deep mountains, further mastering the subtle purport of all books, and authored Expository Marks on the Documents, Charts of Changes through the Ages in the Spring and Autumn, Genealogy of Transmission of the Spring and Autumn, Record of Ancient Regional Offices, Biographies of Mencius's Disciples, Correct Sounds of Chu and Han, Classified Compilation of Music Bureau Poems in one hundred fascicles, Abridged Essentials of Tang Lyric Rules in thirty fascicles, and collected works in sixty fascicles.

sentences.zh: 他如《詩傳科條》、《春秋經說》、《胡氏傳證誤》，皆未脫稿。

translations.literal: Others such as Sections of the Poetry Commentary, Expositions on the Spring and Autumn Classic, and Corrections of Errors in the Hu Clan Commentary—all were not taken from draft.
translations.idiomatic: Others such as Sections of the Poetry Commentary, Expositions on the Spring and Autumn Classic, and Corrections of Errors in the Hu Clan Commentary—all remained unfinished.

sentences.zh: 萊尤喜論文，嘗云：「作文如用兵，兵法有正有奇，正是法度，要部伍分明，奇是不為法度所縛，舉眼之頃，千變萬化，坐作進退擊刺，一時俱起，及其欲止，什伍各還其隊，元不曾亂。」

translations.literal: Lai especially loved discussing essays and once said: 'Composing essays is like employing troops. Military method has orthodox and unorthodox—orthodox is regulation, requiring ranks clearly distinguished; unorthodox is not bound by regulation. In the blink of an eye, a thousand changes and ten thousand transformations—sitting, rising, advancing, retreating, striking, thrusting—all rise at once; when one wishes to stop, squads of five and ten each return to their companies, never disordered in the origin.'
translations.idiomatic: Lai especially loved discussing essays and once said, 'Composing essays is like employing troops. Military method has orthodox and unorthodox forms—orthodox is regulation, requiring ranks clearly distinguished; unorthodox is not bound by regulation. In the blink of an eye come endless changes—sitting, rising, advancing, retreating, striking, thrusting—all rise at once; when one wishes to stop, each squad returns to its place, never disordered.'

sentences.zh: 聞者服之。

translations.literal: Those who heard were convinced.
translations.idiomatic: Those who heard were convinced.

sentences.zh: 貫​​平生極慎許與，每稱萊為絕世之才。

translations.literal: Guan in life was extremely cautious in granting approval, yet always called Lai talent of a vanished age.
translations.idiomatic: Guan in life was extremely cautious in granting approval, yet always called Lai talent of a vanished age.

sentences.zh: 溍晚年謂人曰：「萊之文，嶄絕雄深，類秦、漢間人所作，實非今世之士也。

translations.literal: Jin in his later years told others: 'Lai's writings are towering, unique, heroic, and deep, resembling work of men between Qin and Han—truly not a scholar of this age.
translations.idiomatic: Jin in his later years said, 'Lai's writings are towering, heroic, and deep, resembling work of the Qin and Han era—truly not a scholar of this age.

sentences.zh: 吾縱操觚一世，又安敢及之哉！」

translations.literal: Though I wield the writing brush all my life, how would I dare reach him!'
translations.idiomatic: Though I have wielded the brush all my life, how would I dare compare with him!'

sentences.zh: 其為前輩所推許如此。

translations.literal: Such was the esteem in which elders held him.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which his elders held him.

sentences.zh: 萊以御史薦，調長薌書院山長，未上，卒，年僅四十有四，君子惜之。

translations.literal: Lai was recommended by a censor, transferred to be mountain chief of Changxiang Academy, but before assuming office died at only forty-four; gentlemen regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Lai was recommended by a censor and appointed mountain chief of Changxiang Academy, but before assuming office he died at only forty-four; gentlemen regretted his loss.

sentences.zh: 私諡曰淵穎先生。

translations.literal: His private temple name was Master Yuanying.
translations.idiomatic: His private posthumous title was Master Yuanying.
